title.zh: 卷一百八十 志第一百三十三 食貨下二
title.raw: 卷一百八十 志第一百三十三 食貨下二 Volume 180 Treatises 133: Finance and Economics 2b

sentences.zh: 食貨下二

translations.literal: Finance and Goods, Lower Part Two.
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics 2b.

translations.literal: (Coinage)
translations.idiomatic: (Coinage)

sentences.zh: 錢幣

translations.literal: (Coinage)
translations.idiomatic: (Coinage)

sentences.zh: 錢有銅、鐵二等，而折二、折三、當五、折十，則隨時立製。

translations.literal: Coins had two grades, copper and iron; as for twofold-reduction, threefold-reduction, worth-five, and tenfold-reduction coins, institutions were established as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Coins came in two kinds, copper and iron; denominations such as double-value, triple-value, five-for-one, and tenfold coins were instituted as circumstances demanded.

sentences.zh: 行之久者，唯小平錢。

translations.literal: What circulated for long was only the standard small coin.
translations.idiomatic: Of these, only the standard small-denomination coin remained in circulation for long.

sentences.zh: 夾錫錢最後出，宋之錢法至是而壞。

translations.literal: Tin-adulterated coins came out last; at this point Song coinage law was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The tin-adulterated coins appeared last, and with them the Song monetary system collapsed.

sentences.zh: 蓋自五代以來，相承用唐舊錢，其別鑄者殊鮮。

translations.literal: Generally from the Five Dynasties onward, they continued using Tang old coins; separately cast coins were extremely few.
translations.idiomatic: From the Five Dynasties onward the dynasty largely continued using Tang-era coinage, and fresh minting was rare.

sentences.zh: 太祖初鑄錢，文曰「宋通元寶」。

translations.literal: When Taizu first cast coins, the inscription read "Song Tong Yuan Bao."
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of his reign, Emperor Taizu minted coins inscribed Song Tong Yuan Bao.

sentences.zh: 凡諸州輕小惡錢及鐵鑞錢悉禁之，詔到限一月送官，限滿不送官者罪有差，其私鑄者皆棄市。

translations.literal: All lightweight inferior coins and iron-lead coins in the various prefectures were entirely prohibited; from the date the edict arrived one month was allowed to deliver them to the authorities; those who after the deadline did not deliver them to the authorities were punished in graded penalties; those who privately cast coins were all executed at the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu banned lightweight debased coins and iron-lead alloy coins throughout the empire; people had one month from the edict's arrival to surrender them to the authorities, with graduated penalties for failing to do so, while private minting was punishable by execution.

sentences.zh: 銅錢闌出江南、塞外及南蕃諸國，差定其法，至二貫者徒一年，五貫以上棄市，募告者賞之。

translations.literal: Copper coins illicitly exported to south of the Yangzi, beyond the frontier passes, and to the various southern barbarian countries—graduated penalties were fixed: up to two strings brought one year of penal servitude; five strings or more meant execution at the marketplace; informants were rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Illegal export of copper coin to Jiangnan, beyond the frontier, or to southern foreign states was regulated by a tiered code: up to two strings of cash brought one year of penal servitude, five strings or more meant execution, and informants were rewarded.

sentences.zh: 江南錢不得至江北。

translations.literal: Jiangnan coins were not permitted to reach Jiangbei.
translations.idiomatic: Coin from south of the Yangzi could not be taken north of the river.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，聽仍用鐵錢。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, permission was given to continue using iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Shu, the court allowed iron coin to remain in circulation there.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，詔雅州百丈縣置監冶鑄，禁銅錢入兩川。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao era, an edict ordered that at Baizhang County in Yazhou a mint be established for casting; copper coins entering the Two Sichuan Circuits were prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao reign, a mint was established at Baizhang County in Yazhou, and copper coin was barred from entering the Two Sichuan Circuits.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，始開其禁，而鐵錢不出境，令民輸租及榷利，鐵錢十納銅錢一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, they first lifted that prohibition, but iron coins were not permitted to leave the border; the people were ordered that in paying land tax and monopoly levies, for every ten iron coins one copper coin was to be paid.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4 (979), the copper ban was eased, though iron coin still could not leave the region; for land tax and monopoly dues, one copper coin was required for every ten iron coins.

sentences.zh: 時銅錢已竭，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: At the time copper coins were already exhausted; the people suffered greatly from it.
translations.idiomatic: By then copper coin was already scarce, and the burden on the people was severe.

sentences.zh: 商賈爭以銅錢入川界與民互市，銅錢一得鐵錢十四。

translations.literal: Merchants vied to bring copper coins into the Sichuan border to trade with the people; one copper coin could obtain fourteen iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants rushed copper coin into Sichuan to trade with locals, getting fourteen iron coins for each copper one.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉運副使張諤言：「川峽鐵錢十直銅錢一，輸租即十取二。

translations.literal: The next year, Vice Transport Commissioner Zhang E said: "In the Sichuan gorges ten iron coins are worth one copper coin; for paying rent, one takes two from ten.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Vice Transport Commissioner Zhang E reported: "In Sichuan, ten iron coins equal one copper coin, yet rent collection takes two copper coins from every ten iron coins paid.

sentences.zh: 舊用鐵錢千易銅錢四百，自平蜀，沈倫等悉取銅錢上供，及增鑄鐵錢易民銅錢，益買金銀裝發，頗失裁制，物價滋長，鐵錢彌賤。

translations.literal: Formerly using one thousand iron coins one exchanged for four hundred copper coins; since pacifying Shu, Shen Lun and others entirely took copper coins to supply the court, and moreover increased casting iron coins to exchange for the people's copper coins, further buying gold and silver to dispatch as tribute—greatly losing restraint, prices ever rose, and iron coins became ever cheaper.
translations.idiomatic: He explained that formerly 1,000 iron coins traded for 400 copper coins, but since the Shu conquest Shen Lun and others had drained copper coin for tribute, minted more iron coin to extract copper from the populace, and bought gold and silver for dispatch—all beyond prudent limits, driving up prices and depreciating iron coin further.

sentences.zh: 請市夷人銅，斤給鐵錢千，可以大獲銅鑄錢。

translations.literal: He requested to purchase copper from barbarian Yi people, giving one thousand iron coins per jin, so that copper could be obtained in great quantity to cast coins.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed buying copper from non-Han peoples at 1,000 iron coins per jin to obtain large quantities for minting.

sentences.zh: 民租當輸錢者，許且輸銀絹，候銅錢多，即漸令輸之。」

translations.literal: For the people's rent that should be paid in coin, permission was granted temporarily to pay in silver and silk; when copper coins became plentiful, then gradually order them to pay in coin."
translations.idiomatic: Rent due in coin could temporarily be paid in silver or silk until copper became more plentiful, when coin payment would be phased back in."

sentences.zh: 詔令市夷人銅，斤給鐵錢五百，餘皆從之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered purchasing copper from barbarian Yi people, giving five hundred iron coins per jin; the rest was all accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court authorized buying Yi copper at 500 iron coins per jin (half Zhang's rate) and adopted the rest of his plan.

sentences.zh: 然銅卒難得，而轉運副使聶詠、轉運判官範祥皆言：民樂輸銅錢，請歲遞增一分，後十歲則全取銅錢。

translations.literal: However copper in the end was difficult to obtain, and Vice Transport Commissioner Nie Yong and Transport Assessor Fan Xiang both said: the people are willing to pay copper coins; they requested increasing by one part each year, and after ten years then entirely take copper coins.
translations.idiomatic: Copper remained hard to obtain; Nie Yong and Fan Xiang reported that people would accept paying in copper coin if the requirement increased by one-tenth yearly until full copper payment after ten years.

sentences.zh: 詔如所請。

translations.literal: An edict accorded with what was requested.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 詠祥等因以月俸所得銅錢市與民，厚取其直，於是增及三分，民益以為苦，或發古塚、毀佛像器用，才得銅錢四五，坐罪者甚眾。

translations.literal: Nie Yong, Fan Xiang, and others thereupon used the copper coins from their monthly salaries to sell to the people, heavily taking profit; thus the increase reached three parts; the people came to suffer even more; some exhumed ancient tombs and destroyed Buddha images and utensils, obtaining only four or five copper coins; those convicted were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Nie and Fan then sold their salary copper coin to the public at inflated prices, pushing the annual increase to three-tenths; hardship drove people to rob tombs and melt Buddhist implements for a few coins, and prosecutions mounted.

sentences.zh: 知益州辛仲甫具言其弊，詔使臣吳承勳馳傳審度。

translations.literal: The prefect of Yizhou, Xin Zhongfu, fully stated its evils; an edict sent Commissioner Wu Chengxun by fast relay to investigate and assess.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou prefect Xin Zhongfu detailed the abuses, and Commissioner Wu Chengxun was dispatched post-haste to investigate.

sentences.zh: 仲甫集諸縣令、佐問之，多潛持兩端，莫敢正言。

translations.literal: Zhongfu assembled the various county magistrates and assistants to question them; many secretly hedged both ways, none daring to speak frankly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu summoned county magistrates and aides; most equivocated, fearing to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 仲甫以大誼責之，乃皆言其不便。

translations.literal: Zhongfu reproached them with great righteousness, and then all spoke of its inconvenience.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked them on principle until all admitted the policy was unworkable.

sentences.zh: 承勳復命。

translations.literal: Chengxun reported back.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengxun returned with his report.

sentences.zh: 二年，遂令川峽輸租榷利勿復徵銅錢。

translations.literal: In the second year, they then ordered that in the Sichuan gorges for paying rent and monopoly levies copper coins were no longer to be collected.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign, copper coin collection for rent and monopoly dues in Sichuan was abolished.

sentences.zh: 宋詠祥等皆坐罪免。

translations.literal: Nie Yong, Fan Xiang, and others all were convicted and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Yong, Fan Xiang, and their associates were convicted and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 既而又從西川轉運使劉度之請，官以鐵錢四百易銅錢一百，後竟罷之。

translations.literal: Subsequently they again followed the request of West Sichuan Transport Commissioner Liu Du: the government exchanged four hundred iron coins for one hundred copper coins; later it was ultimately abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on Liu Du's petition as West Sichuan transport commissioner, the state exchanged 400 iron coins for 100 copper coins—a measure eventually revoked.

sentences.zh: 平廣南、江南，亦聽權用舊錢，如川蜀法。

translations.literal: When Guangnan and Jiangnan were pacified, permission was also given provisionally to use old coins, as in the Sichuan-Shu law.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Guangnan and Jiangnan, provisional use of existing coinage was allowed, following the Sichuan model.

sentences.zh: 初，南唐李氏鑄錢，一工為錢千五百，得三十萬貫。

translations.literal: Initially, the Li family of Southern Tang cast coins: one worker produced one thousand five hundred coins, obtaining thirty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Li rulers of Southern Tang minted coin at a rate of 1,500 coins per worker, yielding 300,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，詔升州置監鑄錢，令轉運使按行所部，凡山川之出銅者悉禁民采，並以給官鑄焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended, an edict ordered establishing a mint at Shengzhou for casting coins; transport commissioners were ordered to inspect their jurisdictions; wherever mountains and rivers produced copper, the people were entirely forbidden to mine it, and all was supplied for official casting.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong ordered a mint at Shengzhou and directed transport commissioners to tour their circuits, banning private copper mining and reserving all output for official minting.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，樊若水言：「江南舊用鐵錢，於民非便。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, Fan Ruoshui said: "Jiangnan formerly used iron coins; for the people it was not convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2, Fan Ruoshui argued: "Jiangnan's iron coin was a hardship for the people.

sentences.zh: 今諸州銅錢尚六七十萬緡，虔、吉等州未有銅錢，各發六七萬緡，俾市金帛輕貨上供及博糴穀麥。

translations.literal: Now the various prefectures still have six or seven hundred thousand strings of copper coins; Qian and Ji prefectures and others do not yet have copper coins—each should disburse sixty or seventy thousand strings, enabling purchase of gold, silk, light goods for tribute supply and buying grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: He noted 600,000–700,000 strings of copper coin still in regional treasuries; Qian and Ji prefectures lacked copper coin and should each release 60,000–70,000 strings to buy tribute goods and grain.

sentences.zh: 於昇、鄂饒等州產銅之地，大鑄銅錢，銅錢既不渡江，益出新錢，則民間錢愈多，鐵錢自當不用，悉熔鑄為農器什物，以給江北流民之歸附者。

translations.literal: In Sheng, E, Rao, and other prefectures where copper was produced, cast copper coins on a large scale; since copper coins would no longer cross the river, increasingly issuing new coins, then popular coin would become ever more abundant, iron coins would naturally no longer be used—all melt-cast into farm tools and utensils, to supply the refugees from north of the river who came to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed large-scale minting where copper was mined; keeping new copper coin south of the Yangzi would flood the market, obviate iron coin, and let melted iron be recast as farm tools for resettled refugees from the north.

sentences.zh: 除銅錢渡江之禁。」

translations.literal: Remove the prohibition on copper coins crossing the river."
translations.idiomatic: Lift the ban on moving copper coin across the Yangzi."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [It was] accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 自唐天祐中，兵亂窘乏，以八十五錢為百。

translations.literal: From the Tianyou era of Tang, military chaos and scarcity—eighty-five coins counted as one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang Tianyou (904–907), war and scarcity had made eighty-five coins pass for one hundred.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成中，減五錢，漢乾祐初，復減三錢。

translations.literal: In the Later Tang Tiancheng era, five coins were reduced; at the beginning of Later Han Gan You, three coins were again reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tang Tiancheng cut that to eighty; early Later Han Gan You to seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 宋初，凡輸官者亦用八十或八十五為百，然諸州私用則各隨其俗，至有以四十八錢為百者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, all payments to the government also used eighty or eighty-five as one hundred; however, in private use among the various prefectures each followed its local custom, to the point of some using forty-eight coins as one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Early Song official payments still counted eighty or eighty-five as one hundred, but private usage varied by region, some places as low as forty-eight per hundred.

sentences.zh: 至是，詔所在用七十七錢為百。

translations.literal: At this time, an edict ordered that everywhere seventy-seven coins would be used as one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict standardized seventy-seven coins as one hundred everywhere.

sentences.zh: 西北邊內屬戎人，多齎貨帛於秦、階州易銅錢出塞，銷鑄為器。

translations.literal: On the northwest frontier, affiliated Rong barbarians mostly brought goods and cloth to Qin and Jie prefectures to exchange for copper coins and export them beyond the pass, melting and casting them into utensils.
translations.idiomatic: Affiliated frontier peoples often traded goods for copper coin at Qin and Jie prefectures, smuggled it beyond the border, and melted it into utensils.

sentences.zh: 乃詔吏民闌出銅錢百已上論罪，至五貫以上送闕下。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict: officials and commoners illicitly exporting one hundred or more copper coins would be prosecuted; five strings or more were sent to the capital for trial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict penalized illegal export of 100 or more copper coins, with cases of five strings or more sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 舊饒州永平監歲鑄錢六萬貫，平江南，增為七萬貫，而銅、鉛、錫常不給。

translations.literal: Formerly Yongping Mint in Raozhou annually cast sixty thousand strings; after pacifying Jiangnan, it was increased to seventy thousand strings, but copper, lead, and tin were constantly insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping Mint at Raozhou had cast 60,000 strings yearly, raised to 70,000 after Jiangnan's pacification, but copper, lead, and tin supplies were chronically short.

sentences.zh: 轉運使張齊賢訪求得南唐承旨丁釗，能知饒、信等州山谷產銅、鉛、錫，乃便宜調民采取；

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Zhang Qixian sought and obtained Ding Zhao, former Director of Southern Tang, who knew where copper, lead, and tin were produced in the mountains and valleys of Raozhou, Xinzhou, and other prefectures; thereupon, as expedient, the people were mobilized to extract them;
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Zhang Qixian found Ding Zhao, a former Southern Tang court scholar who knew copper, lead, and tin deposits in Raozhou and Xinzhou, and mobilized the populace to mine them.

sentences.zh: 且詢舊鑄法，惟永平用唐開元錢料最善，即詣闕麵陳。

translations.literal: Moreover he inquired into the old casting method; only Yongping used Tang Kaiyuan coin alloy most excellently; he then went to court and stated it in person.
translations.idiomatic: He also learned that Yongping's Tang Kaiyuan alloy formula was best and presented this at court in person.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔增市鉛、錫、炭價，於是得銅八十一萬斤、鉛三十六萬斤、錫十六萬斤，歲鑄錢三十萬貫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict increased purchase prices for lead, tin, and charcoal; thereby obtaining 810,000 jin of copper, 360,000 jin of lead, 160,000 jin of tin; annually casting 300,000 strings.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, higher purchase prices for lead, tin, and charcoal yielded 810,000 jin of copper, 360,000 jin of lead, and 160,000 jin of tin, enabling annual output of 300,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 補釗殿前承旨，領三州銅山。

translations.literal: Ding Zhao was appointed Palace Director and put in charge of the copper mountains of the three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Zhao was appointed palace director and placed in charge of copper mining across three prefectures.

sentences.zh: 然民間猶雜用舊大小錢。

translations.literal: However among the people old large and small coins were still mixed in use.
translations.idiomatic: Old large and small coins nonetheless continued to circulate privately.

sentences.zh: 是時，以福建銅錢數少，令建州鑄大鐵錢並行，尋罷鑄，而官私所有鐵錢十萬貫，不出州境，每千錢與銅錢七百七十等，外邑鄰兩浙者亦不用。

translations.literal: At this time, because Fujian copper coins were few in number, Jianzhou was ordered to cast large iron coins for concurrent circulation; soon casting was stopped, but government and private iron coins totaling one hundred thousand strings did not leave the prefecture border; every thousand coins were equivalent to seven hundred seventy copper coins; outer districts neighboring the Two Zhe circuits also did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fujian lacked copper coin, Jianzhou briefly minted large iron coin for parallel circulation; minting ceased, but 100,000 strings of iron coin remained confined to the prefecture, valued at 770 copper coins per thousand, unused even in neighboring Two-Zhe districts.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，令江南諸州官庫所貯雜錢，每貫及四斤半者送闕下，不及者銷毀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, the various Jiangnan prefectures' official treasuries' stored miscellaneous coins—each string reaching four jin and a half was sent to the capital; those not reaching it were melted and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongxi, Jiangnan treasuries were to send strings weighing at least four and a half jin to the capital and melt lighter mixed coin.

sentences.zh: 民間惡錢尚多，復申乾德之禁，稍峻其法。

translations.literal: Among the people inferior coins were still numerous; the Qiande prohibitions were again proclaimed, and the law was somewhat tightened.
translations.idiomatic: Debasing private coin remained widespread, so Taizu's Qiande prohibitions were reissued with stricter enforcement.

sentences.zh: 京城居民蓄銅器者，限兩月悉送官。

translations.literal: Capital residents storing copper vessels—within two months all were to be delivered to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Capital residents holding copper vessels had two months to surrender them to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，內侍蕭延皓使嶺南還，以民間私鑄三等錢來上，且言多與蠻人貿易，侵敗禁法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duangong, Palace Attendant Xiao Yanhao, returning from a mission to Lingnan, presented privately cast third-grade coins from among the people, and added many were traded with barbarian Man people, violating and corrupting prohibitory law.
translations.idiomatic: In Duangong 1, palace attendant Xiao Yanhao returned from Lingnan with samples of privately cast third-grade coin, reporting extensive trade with indigenous peoples in violation of the law.

sentences.zh: 因詔察民私鑄及銷鎔好錢作薄惡錢者，並棄市；

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered investigation of people's private casting and melting good coins to make thin inferior coins—all executed at the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: An edict targeted private minting and melting good coin into debased thin coin—both punishable by execution;

sentences.zh: 輒以新惡錢與蠻人博易者，抵罪。

translations.literal: Those who rashly used newly made inferior coins to trade with barbarian Man people would be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Trading fresh debased coin with indigenous peoples was also criminalized.

sentences.zh: 江北諸州所用錢非甚薄惡者，新舊大小兼用。

translations.literal: In the various prefectures north of the river, coins used that were not very thin and inferior—old and new, large and small, were used together.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yangzi, coin that was not severely debased could circulate old and new, large and small, together.

sentences.zh: 江南雖用舊大錢，淳化四年，乃詔每貫及前詔斤數、有官監字號者皆許用，不分新舊。

translations.literal: Jiangnan although used old large coins, in the fourth year of Chunhua, an edict then ordered: each string reaching the weight of previous edicts and bearing official mint marks—all permitted for use, not distinguishing old from new.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiangnan still used old large coin, Chunhua 4 decreed that any string meeting prior weight standards and bearing official mint marks was valid regardless of age.

sentences.zh: 先是，淳化二年，宗正少卿趙安易言：嘗使蜀，見所用鐵錢至輕，市羅一匹，為錢二萬。

translations.literal: Previously, in the second year of Chunhua, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Zhao Anyi said: I once served as envoy to Shu and saw iron coins used there were extremely light; buying one bolt of gauze required twenty thousand coins.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Chunhua 2, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Zhao Anyi reported from a mission to Shu that iron coin there was so light one bolt of gauze cost 20,000 coins.

sentences.zh: 堅請改鑄一當十大錢，御書錢式，遣詣川峽路諸州冶鑄，所在並為御書錢監；

translations.literal: He firmly requested recasting ten-for-one large coins; the emperor personally wrote the coin model; officials were dispatched to the various prefectures of the Sichuan gorges route to smelt and cast; everywhere they became imperial-script coin mints;
translations.idiomatic: He urged minting large ten-for-one iron coin; the emperor wrote the design, and imperial-script mints were established throughout Sichuan;

sentences.zh: 諸州舊貯小鐵錢悉輦送官。

translations.literal: The various prefectures' formerly stored small iron coins were all carted and delivered to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Existing stores of small iron coin were carted to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 民間小錢許送監，計數給以大錢；

translations.literal: Among the people, small coins were permitted to be delivered to the mint; counted, large coins were given in exchange;
translations.idiomatic: The public could surrender small coin to mints for large coin at the prescribed rate;

sentences.zh: 若改鑄未集，許民大小兼用。

translations.literal: If recasting was not yet complete, the people were permitted to use large and small together.
translations.idiomatic: Until recoinage was complete, large and small coin could circulate together.

sentences.zh: 既而一歲才成三千餘貫，眾皆以為不便。

translations.literal: Before long, in one year only a little over three thousand strings were completed; all considered it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: After a year only 3,000-odd strings had been minted, and the scheme was universally deemed impractical.

sentences.zh: 會安易入奏事，因留不遣，遂罷冶鑄。

translations.literal: When Anyi happened to enter court to report on affairs, he was thereupon detained and not sent back; then smelting and casting was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Anyi came to court, he was kept at the capital and minting was halted.

sentences.zh: 五年，安易復請，不許。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Anyi again requested; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his renewed petition was denied.

sentences.zh: 第令川峽仍以銅錢一當鐵錢十。

translations.literal: Only ordered that in the Sichuan gorges one copper coin still counted as ten iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: The court merely reaffirmed the exchange rate of one copper coin to ten iron coins in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 荊湖、嶺南民輸稅須大錢，民以小錢二或三易大錢一，官屬以奉錢易於民以規利。

translations.literal: In Jinghu and Lingnan the people paying taxes required large coins; the people exchanged two or three small coins for one large coin; officials and clerks used stipend money to exchange with the people to seek profit.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghu and Lingnan, taxes had to be paid in large coin; commoners traded two or three small coins for one large coin, while officials exploited the exchange using their stipend coin for profit.

sentences.zh: 詔自今吏受民輸，但常所通行錢勿卻，官吏毋得以奉錢換易。

translations.literal: An edict: from now when officials receive people's payments, only the coin ordinarily circulating must not be refused; officials and clerks must not use stipend money to exchange.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade officials from refusing legally circulating coin or swapping stipend money with taxpayers for profit.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，始禁道、賀州錫，官益其價市之，以給諸路鑄錢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, tin from Dao and He prefectures was first prohibited to private trade; the government increased its price to purchase it, to supply the various circuits' coin casting.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 2, private tin trade from Dao and He prefectures was banned; the state bought tin at premium prices to supply mints on various circuits.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，又申新小錢之禁，令官置場盡市之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, the prohibition on new small coins was again proclaimed; officials were ordered to establish markets to buy them all.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping, debased new small coin was again banned and bought up at official depots.

sentences.zh: 舊犯銅禁，七斤以上處死，奏裁多蒙減斷，然待報常淹緩。

translations.literal: Formerly violating the copper prohibition—seven jin or more was punished by death; memorials for imperial decision often received reduced sentences, but awaiting report was often slow and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly copper violations of seven jin or more carried the death penalty, though imperial review often commuted sentences—a process that delayed justice.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔滿五十斤以上取裁，餘從第減。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict: fifty jin or more required imperial decision; the rest followed graduated reduction.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, only offenses of fifty jin or more required imperial review; lesser amounts received graded reduction.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，詔曰：「鼓鑄錢刀，素有程限，憫其勞苦，特示矜寬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, an edict said: "Beating and casting coin knives—there have always been quota limits; commiserating their labor and hardship, specially showing compassionate leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde 4: "Coin minters have always faced production quotas; out of sympathy for their labor, We show special forbearance.

sentences.zh: 自今五月一日至八月一日止收半功，本司每歲量支率分錢以備醫藥。」

translations.literal: From now the first day of the fifth month to the first day of the eighth month only half output is collected; this office each year will measure and disburse proportional funds to prepare medicine."
translations.idiomatic: From the first of the fifth month through the first of the eighth month, only half the quota applies; the mint bureau will allocate funds yearly for medical supplies."

sentences.zh: 十二月，令鑄匠每旬停作一日。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, coin craftsmen were ordered one day off each ten-day period.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, minters were granted one day off every ten-day period.

sentences.zh: 天禧三年，詔：犯銅、鍮石，悉免極刑。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianxi, an edict: violating copper and brass prohibitions—all exempted from extreme punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi 3 exempted copper and brass violations from capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 時銅錢有四監：饒州曰永平，池州曰永豐，江州曰廣寧，建州曰豐國。

translations.literal: At the time copper coins had four mints: Raozhou called Yongping, Chizhou called Yongfeng, Jiangzhou called Guangning, Jianzhou called Fengguo.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were four copper mints: Yongping in Raozhou, Yongfeng in Chizhou, Guangning in Jiangzhou, and Fengguo in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 京師、升鄂杭州、南安軍舊皆有監，後廢之。

translations.literal: The capital, Sheng-E-Hang prefectures, and Nan'an Commandery formerly all had mints; later they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Mints at the capital, Shengzhou, Ezhou, Hangzhou, and Nan'an Commandery had all been closed.

sentences.zh: 凡鑄錢用銅三斤十兩，鉛一斤八兩，錫八兩，得錢千，重五斤。

translations.literal: Generally casting coins used three jin ten liang of copper, one jin eight liang of lead, eight liang of tin, obtaining one thousand coins weighing five jin.
translations.idiomatic: Standard alloy was three jin ten liang copper, one jin eight liang lead, and eight liang tin per thousand coins weighing five jin total.

sentences.zh: 唯建州增銅五兩，減鉛如其數。

translations.literal: Only Jianzhou increased copper by five liang and reduced lead by the same amount.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhou alone added five liang of copper and reduced lead accordingly.

sentences.zh: 至道中，歲鑄八十萬貫；

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era, annually casting eight hundred thousand strings;
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhidao, annual output reached 800,000 strings;

sentences.zh: 景德中，增至一百八十三萬貫。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era, it increased to one million eight hundred thirty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingde it rose to 1,830,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符後，銅坑多不發。

translations.literal: After Dazhong Xiangfu, copper mines mostly were not opened.
translations.idiomatic: After Dazhong Xiangfu, many copper mines ceased production.

sentences.zh: 天禧末，鑄一百五萬貫。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianxi, casting one million five hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: By late Tianxi, minting had fallen to 1,500,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 鐵錢有三監：邛州曰惠民，嘉州曰豐遠，興州曰濟眾。

translations.literal: Iron coins had three mints: Qiongzhou called Huimin, Jiazhou called Fengyuan, Xingzhou called Jizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Iron coin had three mints: Huimin in Qiongzhou, Fengyuan in Jiazhou, and Jizhong in Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 益州、雅州舊亦有監，後並廢。

translations.literal: Yizhou and Yazhou formerly also had mints; later all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Former mints at Yizhou and Yazhou were also closed.

sentences.zh: 大錢貫十二斤十兩，以準銅錢。

translations.literal: Large coins—a string weighed twelve jin ten liang, to match copper coins.
translations.idiomatic: Large iron coin strings weighed twelve jin ten liang, equivalent to copper coin in value.

sentences.zh: 嘉、邛二州所鑄錢，貫二十五斤八兩，銅錢一當小鐵錢十兼用。

translations.literal: Coins cast by Jia and Qiong two prefectures—a string weighed twenty-five jin eight liang; one copper coin counted as ten small iron coins, used together.
translations.idiomatic: Coin from Jia and Qiong weighed twenty-five jin eight liang per string; one copper coin equaled ten small iron coins, both circulating.

sentences.zh: 後以鐵重，多盜熔為器，每二十五斤鬻之直二千。

translations.literal: Later because iron was heavy, many secretly melted it into utensils; every twenty-five jin sold for two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because iron was so heavy, much was illicitly melted into utensils—a twenty-five-jin lot fetching 2,000 coins' worth.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符七年，知益州淩策言：「錢輕則易齎，鐵少則鎔者鮮利。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Prefect of Yizhou Ling Ce said: "If coins are lighter they are easier to carry; if iron is less, those who melt have little profit."
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 7, Yizhou prefect Ling Ce argued: "Lighter coin is easier to carry, and less iron means less profit in illicit melting."

sentences.zh: 於是詔減景德之制，其見使舊錢仍用如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict reduced the Jingde standard; existing old coins in circulation still were used as before.
translations.idiomatic: The court reduced the Jingde standard while allowing existing coin to remain in circulation.

sentences.zh: 歲鑄總二十一萬貫，諸路錢歲輸京師，四方由此錢重而貨輕。

translations.literal: Annual casting totaled two hundred ten thousand strings; coin from the various circuits yearly was transported to the capital; throughout the realm thereby coin was heavy and goods light.
translations.idiomatic: Annual iron coin output totaled 210,000 strings; as coin from all circuits flowed to the capital, money grew heavy and goods cheap nationwide.

sentences.zh: 景祐初，詔三司以江東、福建、廣南盛輸緡錢合三十餘萬易為金帛，錢流民間。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyou, an edict ordered the Three Departments to take Jiangdong, Fujian, and Guangnan's surplus tribute of coin strings totaling more than three hundred thousand and exchange for gold and silk, so coin would flow among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingyou, the Three Departments were ordered to convert over 300,000 strings of surplus tribute coin from Jiangdong, Fujian, and Guangnan into gold and silk, releasing coin into circulation.

sentences.zh: 許申為三司度支判官，建議以藥化鐵與銅雜鑄，輕重如銅錢法，銅居三分，鐵六分，皆有奇贏，亦得錢千，費省而利厚。

translations.literal: Xu Shen, as Revenue Assessor of the Three Departments, proposed using chemical treatment to refine iron and mix-cast with copper; weight like the copper coin standard; copper occupying three parts, iron six parts—all with surplus gain; also obtaining one thousand coins; expense saved and profit thick.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Assessor Xu Shen proposed treating iron chemically and alloying it with copper in a 3:6 ratio by weight to the copper-coin standard, yielding 1,000 coins at lower cost and higher profit.

sentences.zh: 詔申用其法鑄於京師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shen to use his method to cast at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court authorized Xu Shen to trial his method at the capital.

sentences.zh: 大率鑄錢雜鉛、錫，則其液流速而易成，申雜以鐵，流澀而多不就，工人苦之。

translations.literal: Generally casting coins mixed with lead and tin—their liquid flowed swiftly and was easy to complete; Shen mixed with iron—the flow was sluggish and many did not succeed; the workers suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinarily adding lead and tin made the molten alloy flow freely and cast easily; Shen's iron mixture flowed sluggishly, failed often, and tormented the workers.

sentences.zh: 初命申鑄萬緡，逾月裁得萬錢。

translations.literal: At first [they] ordered Shen to cast ten thousand strings of cash; after more than a month he had produced only ten thousand coins.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was first ordered to cast ten thousand strings of cash, but after more than a month had minted only ten thousand coins.

sentences.zh: 申性詭譎，少成事，自度言無效，乃求為江東轉運使，欲用其法於江州。

translations.literal: Shen's nature was treacherous and deceitful; he seldom accomplished anything. Judging that his words had no effect, he then sought appointment as Jiangdong transport commissioner, wishing to apply his method at Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was shifty and seldom succeeded at anything. Concluding that he would never persuade the court at the capital, he asked to be made transport commissioner for Jiangdong so he could trial his method at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之，因詔申即江州鑄百萬緡，毋漏其法。

translations.literal: The court assented, and accordingly issued an edict ordering Shen to cast one million strings of cash right at Jiang Prefecture, not divulging his method.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed and ordered Shen to mint one million strings at Jiangzhou on the spot, while keeping his technique secret.

sentences.zh: 中外知其非是，而宰相主之，卒無成功。

translations.literal: Within and outside the court knew this was wrong, but the chief minister upheld it; in the end there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone at court and beyond knew the scheme was unsound, yet the chief minister stood behind it, and in the end it failed utterly.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗改元太平興國，更鑄：「太平通寶」，淳化更鑄，又親書「淳化元寶」，作真、行、草三體。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Taizong changed the era name to Taiping Xingguo, he re-cast: "Taiping Tongbao"; when [the era] changed to Chunhua he re-cast again, and personally wrote "Chunhua Yuanbao," making the regular, running, and cursive script forms.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, when Taizong adopted the era name Taiping Xingguo, new coins were cast reading "Taiping Tongbao." After the Chunhua era began, he had coins recast again and personally wrote "Chunhua Yuanbao" in regular, running, and cursive scripts.

sentences.zh: 後改元更鑄，皆曰「元寶」，而冠以年號，至是改元寶元，文當曰「寶元元寶」，仁宗特命以「皇宋通寶」為文，慶曆以後，復冠以年號如舊。

translations.literal: Later, on each change of era they re-cast; all were called "Yuanbao," with the era name prefixed. At this time the era was changed to Baoyuan—textually it should read "Baoyuan Yuanbao"—but Emperor Renzong specially ordered "Huang Song Tongbao" as the inscription; after Qingli, the era name was again prefixed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter each new reign title brought new casting; all bore the word Yuanbao with the era name prefixed. When the era Baoyuan began, the legend ought to have read "Baoyuan Yuanbao," but Renzong specifically ordered "Imperial Song Universal Treasure" instead. After Qingli, prefixes resumed as before.

sentences.zh: 自天聖以來，毀錢鑄鍾及為銅器，皆有禁。

translations.literal: Since the Tiansheng era, destroying coins to cast bells and to make copper vessels—both were prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tiansheng era onward, melting coins to cast bells or fashion copperware was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 慶曆初，闌出銅錢，視舊法第加其罪，錢千，為首者抵死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingli, smuggling copper cash out—compared with the old law only the penalties were increased: for one thousand coins, the ringleader was punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingli, penalties for illicit export of copper cash were stiffened under the old statutes: for one thousand coins, the chief offender faced execution.

sentences.zh: 五年，泉州青陽鐵冶大發，轉運使高易簡不俟詔，置鐵錢務於泉，欲移銅錢於內地；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the iron smelter at Qingyang in Quan Prefecture greatly flourished; transport commissioner Gao Yijian, without awaiting an edict, established an iron cash office at Quan, wishing to shift copper cash inland;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, iron production boomed at Qingyang in Quanzhou. Transport commissioner Gao Yijian, acting without imperial authorization, set up an iron-coin bureau in Quanzhou, hoping to draw copper cash inland;

sentences.zh: 梓州路轉運使崔輔、判官張固亦請即廣安軍魚子鐵山采礦炭，置監於合州，並銷舊小錢以鑄減輕大錢，未得報，先移合州相地置監。

translations.literal: Zizhou Circuit transport commissioner Cui Fu and aide Zhang Gu also requested immediately to mine ore and coal at Yuzi Iron Mountain in Guangan Army, establish a mint at He Prefecture, and concurrently melt down old small coins to cast lightened large coins; before receiving a reply, they first moved to He Prefecture to survey a site and establish a mint.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Fu, transport commissioner of Zizhou Circuit, and his aide Zhang Gu likewise proposed mining ore and coal at Yuzi Iron Mountain in Guangan Army, opening a mint in Hezhou, and recoining worn small cash into lighter large coins. Before any answer came, they moved into Hezhou to scout a site and set up the mint.

sentences.zh: 州以上聞，朝廷以易簡、輔、固為擅鑄錢，皆坐貶。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported upward; the court regarded Yijian, Fu, and Gu as having cast coins on their own authority—all were sentenced to demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported the matter. The court held Yijian, Fu, and Gu guilty of unauthorized coinage and demoted them all.

sentences.zh: 軍興，陝西移用不足，始用知商州皮仲容議，采洛南縣紅崖山、虢州青水冶青銅，置阜民、朱陽二監鑄錢。

translations.literal: When war began, transfers for use in Shaanxi were insufficient; they first adopted the proposal of Shang Prefecture prefect Pi Zhongrong, mining bronze at Hongya Mountain in Luonan County and at Qingshui in Guo Prefecture, establishing the Fumin and Zhuyang mints to cast cash.
translations.idiomatic: With the outbreak of war, supplies for Shaanxi ran short. The court first took up a plan from Shangzhou prefect Pi Zhongrong: mine bronze at Hongya Mountain in Luonan County and at Qingshui in Guozhou, and establish the Fumin and Zhuyang mints.

sentences.zh: 既而陝西都轉運使張奎、知永興軍範雍請鑄大銅錢與小錢兼行，大錢一當小錢十；

translations.literal: Subsequently Shaanxi chief transport commissioner Zhang Kui and Yongxing Army prefect Fan Yong requested casting large copper coins to circulate together with small coins—one large coin equal to ten small coins;
translations.idiomatic: Later, Shaanxi chief transport commissioner Zhang Kui and Yongxing prefect Fan Yong urged minting large copper cash alongside small coin, at a rate of one large to ten small;

sentences.zh: 又請因晉州積鐵鑄小錢。

translations.literal: They also requested using accumulated iron at Jin Prefecture to cast small coins.
translations.idiomatic: They also asked to mint small coin from stockpiled iron in Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 及奎徙河東，又鑄大鐵錢於晉、澤二州，亦以一當十，助關中軍費。

translations.literal: When Kui was transferred to Hedong, he again cast large iron coins in Jin and Ze Prefectures, also at one-for-ten, to assist Guanzhong military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Kui moved to Hedong, he had large iron coins cast in Jin and Ze prefectures, likewise at one-to-ten, to help pay Guanzhong's war costs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，三司奏罷河東鑄大鐵錢，而陝西復采儀州竹尖嶺黃銅，置博濟監鑄大錢。

translations.literal: Before long, the Bureau of Revenue memorialized to stop casting large iron coins in Hedong, while Shaanxi again mined yellow bronze at Zhujian Ridge in Yi Prefecture and established the Boji mint to cast large coins.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Bureau of Revenue moved to halt large iron coinage in Hedong, while Shaanxi reopened mining at Zhujian Ridge in Yizhou for yellow bronze and set up the Boji mint for large coins.

sentences.zh: 因敕江南鑄大銅錢，而江、池、饒、儀、虢又鑄小鐵錢，悉輦致關中。

translations.literal: Accordingly an edict ordered Jiangnan to cast large copper coins, while Jiang, Chi, Rao, Yi, and Guo also cast small iron coins—all were carted to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then called for large copper coins in Jiangnan, while Jiang, Chi, Rao, Yi, and Guo minted small iron cash, all of which was hauled to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 數州錢雜行，大約小銅錢三可鑄當十大銅錢一，以故民間盜鑄者眾，錢文大亂，物價翔踴，公私患之。

translations.literal: Coins of several prefectures circulated in mixture; roughly three small copper coins could be cast into one large copper coin worth ten; for this reason illicit casting in the populace was numerous, coin types greatly chaotic, prices soared, and public and private parties were distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Cash from several prefectures mingled in circulation. Roughly three small copper coins could be illegally recast as one large ten-for-one piece, so counterfeiting flourished, denominations plunged into chaos, prices surged, and officials and commoners alike suffered.

sentences.zh: 於是奎復奏晉、澤、石三州及威勝軍日鑄小鐵錢，獨留用河東。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kui again memorialized that Jin, Ze, and Shi Prefectures and Weisheng Army should cast small iron coins daily, to be kept for use only in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kui then urged daily minting of small iron cash in Jin, Ze, and Shi prefectures and Weisheng Army, reserved for use within Hedong alone.

sentences.zh: 河東鐵錢既行，盜鑄獲利什六，錢輕貨重，患如陝西。

translations.literal: Once Hedong iron coins circulated, illicit casting yielded profit of six-tenths; coins were light and goods heavy—the distress was like Shaanxi's.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hedong iron cash entered circulation, counterfeiting returned a profit of sixty percent; money grew light and goods dear, with woes matching Shaanxi's.

sentences.zh: 知并州鄭戩請河東鐵錢以二當銅錢一，行之一年，又以三當一或以五當一，罷官爐日鑄，且行舊錢。

translations.literal: Bing Prefecture prefect Zheng Jian requested that Hedong iron coins be valued at two for one copper coin; after one year in circulation, then three-for-one or five-for-one, stop daily casting at government furnaces, and for the time being use old coins.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou prefect Zheng Jian proposed revaluing Hedong iron cash at two to one against copper coin. After a year he would shift to three-to-one or five-to-one, suspend daily operation of government mints, and rely on existing stock.

sentences.zh: 而契丹亦鑄鐵錢，易並邊銅錢。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Khitan also cast iron coins, exchanging for copper coins on the Bingzhou frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan minted iron cash as well, trading it for copper coin along the Bingzhou border.

sentences.zh: 慶曆末，葉清臣為三司使，與學士張方平等上陝西錢議，曰：「關中用大錢，本以縣官取利太多，致奸人盜鑄，其用日輕。

translations.literal: Late in Qingli, Ye Qingchen was Bureau of Revenue commissioner; with academician Zhang Fangping and others he submitted a memorial on Shaanxi coinage, saying: "In Guanzhong large coins were used originally because the government took too much profit, causing scoundrels to cast illicitly; their purchasing power daily grew lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Qingli, Ye Qingchen as Bureau of Revenue commissioner joined Academician Zhang Fangping and others in a memorial on Shaanxi currency: "Large coin in Guanzhong was adopted because the state sought excessive seigniorage, inviting counterfeiting and steady debasement.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，皆虛高物估，始增直於下，終取償於上，縣官雖有折當之虛名，乃受虧損之實害。

translations.literal: In recent years all have inflated appraisals of goods—first adding value below, finally recovering payment above; the government though having the empty name of exchange-rate adjustment, in fact suffers real loss.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years officials have inflated valuations—padding prices at the bottom only to claw them back at the top. The state keeps the hollow title of adjusted exchange rates while absorbing real losses.

sentences.zh: 救弊不先自損，則法未易行。

translations.literal: To remedy abuse without first accepting loss oneself—then the law is not easy to implement.
translations.idiomatic: Reform cannot succeed unless the state accepts sacrifice first.

sentences.zh: 請以江南、儀商等州大銅錢一當小錢三，小鐵錢三當銅錢一，河東小鐵錢如陝西，亦以三當一，且罷官所置爐。」

translations.literal: We request that in Jiangnan, Yi, Shang, and other prefectures one large copper coin equal three small coins; three small iron coins equal one copper coin; Hedong small iron coins like Shaanxi—also three for one; and moreover abolish government-established furnaces."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that large copper cash in Jiangnan, Yizhou, Shangzhou, and elsewhere be valued at one to three small coin; small iron cash at three to one copper; Hedong iron cash at the Shaanxi rate of three to one; and that all government mints be shut down."

sentences.zh: 自是奸人稍無利，猶未能絕濫錢。

translations.literal: From this scoundrels gradually had no profit, yet they still could not fully stop debased coin.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiters found fewer profits afterward, yet debased coin could not be eliminated entirely.

sentences.zh: 其後，詔商州罷鑄青黃銅錢，又令陝西大銅錢、大鐵錢皆以一當二，盜鑄乃止。

translations.literal: Afterward, an edict ordered Shang Prefecture to stop casting green and yellow bronze coins; also commanded that in Shaanxi large copper and large iron coins all be one-for-two; illicit casting then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Shangzhou was ordered to stop minting green and yellow bronze cash, and large copper and iron coins in Shaanxi were revalued at one-for-two, whereupon counterfeiting stopped.

sentences.zh: 然令數變，兵民耗於資用，類多谘怨，久之始定。

translations.literal: Yet orders changed frequently; soldiers and civilians were depleted in resources, mostly complained, and only after long time did things settle.
translations.idiomatic: Orders kept changing, however, draining soldiers and civilians alike, and complaints were widespread before stability came at last.

sentences.zh: 方大錢之行，有劉羲叟者語人曰：「是於周景王所鑄無異，上其感心腹之疾乎。」

translations.literal: While large coins were circulating, one Liu Yisou told people: "This is no different from what King Jing of Zhou cast—is not the Emperor afflicted with an illness of the heart and viscera?"
translations.idiomatic: While large coin circulated, a man named Liu Yisou remarked: "This is no different from the coin King Jing of Zhou minted. Surely the Emperor suffers an ailment of the heart?"

sentences.zh: 已而果然，語在本傳。

translations.literal: Before long it proved so—the account is in his basic biography.
translations.idiomatic: And so it proved; the story appears in his biography.

sentences.zh: 時興元府西縣增置濟遠監。

translations.literal: At that time Jiyuan Mint was additionally established in Xi County, Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Jiyuan mint was added in Xi County of Xingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 而韶州天興銅大發，歲采二十五萬斤，詔即其州置永通監。

translations.literal: Meanwhile copper at Tianxing in Shao Prefecture greatly increased; two hundred fifty thousand jin were mined yearly; an edict ordered establishing the Yongtong Mint right in that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Copper production at Tianxing in Shaozhou meanwhile surged to two hundred fifty thousand jin a year, and the court established the Yongtong mint there.

sentences.zh: 後濟遠監廢，儀州博濟監既廢復置。

translations.literal: Later Jiyuan Mint was abolished; Boji Mint in Yi Prefecture, once abolished, was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiyuan mint was later closed, while the Boji mint in Yizhou, once shut down, was reopened.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，饒、池、江、建、韶五州鑄錢百四十六萬緡，嘉、邛、興三州鑄大鐵錢二十七萬緡。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era, Rao, Chi, Jiang, Jian, and Shao—five prefectures—cast 1.46 million strings of cash; Jia, Qiong, and Xing—three prefectures—cast 270,000 strings of large iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou, five prefectures—Rao, Chi, Jiang, Jian, and Shao—minted 1.46 million strings of cash, while Jia, Qiong, and Xing minted 270,000 strings of large iron coin.

sentences.zh: 至治平中，饒、池、江、建、韶、儀六州鑄錢百七十萬緡，而嘉、邛以率買鐵炭為擾，自嘉祐四年停鑄十年，以休民力。

translations.literal: By the Zhiping era, Rao, Chi, Jiang, Jian, Shao, and Yi—six prefectures—cast 1.7 million strings; but Jia and Qiong, because compulsory purchase of iron and coal was oppressive, from the fourth year of Jiayou ceased casting for ten years, to rest the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhiping, six prefectures—Rao, Chi, Jiang, Jian, Shao, and Yi—were minting 1.7 million strings. Jia and Qiong halted casting for ten years from Jiayou 4 because forced requisition of iron and coal had become intolerable, giving the populace respite.

sentences.zh: 至是，獨興州鑄錢三萬緡。

translations.literal: At this time, only Xing Prefecture cast 30,000 strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: By then only Xingzhou still minted, at thirty thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，同、華二州積小鐵錢凡四十萬緡，詔賜河東，以鐵償之。

translations.literal: Early in Xining, Tong and Hua Prefectures had accumulated small iron coins totaling 400,000 strings; an edict granted them to Hedong, repaying with iron.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining, Tong and Hua prefectures held four hundred thousand strings of small iron cash in surplus; the court transferred it to Hedong and compensated with iron.

sentences.zh: 四年，陝西轉運副使皮公弼奏：「自行當二錢，銅費相當，盜鑄衰息。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Shaanxi vice transport commissioner Pi Gongbi memorialized: "Since circulating value-two coins, copper costs are equivalent; illicit casting has declined and abated.
translations.idiomatic: In year four, Shaanxi vice transport commissioner Pi Gongbi reported: "Since value-two coin entered circulation, copper costs have matched face value and counterfeiting has waned.

sentences.zh: 請以舊銅鉛盡鑄。」

translations.literal: We request casting all from old copper and lead."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all remaining copper and lead stock be coined."

sentences.zh: 詔聽之。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是折二錢遂行於天下。

translations.literal: From this value-two coins then circulated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Value-two coin thereafter circulated empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 京西轉運使吳幾復建議：郢、唐、均、房、金五州多林木，而銅鉛積於淮南，若由襄、郢轉致郢、唐等州置監鑄錢，可以紓錢重之弊。

translations.literal: Jingxi transport commissioner Wu Jifu proposed: Ying, Tang, Jun, Fang, and Jin—five prefectures—have abundant forest; copper and lead accumulate in Huainan; if transported via Xiang and Ying to Ying, Tang, and other prefectures to establish mints and cast coins, this could relieve the ill of heavy coin [scarcity].
translations.idiomatic: Jingxi transport commissioner Wu Jifu suggested that Ying, Tang, Jun, Fang, and Jin—wood-rich prefectures—could receive copper and lead stockpiled in Huainan via Xiang and Ying routes, open mints locally, and ease the cash shortage.

sentences.zh: 神宗是之，而王安石沮之，其議遂寢。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong approved it, but Wang Anshi obstructed it; the proposal then lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong favored the plan, but Wang Anshi blocked it, and the proposal died.

sentences.zh: 後乃詔京西、淮南、兩浙、江西、荊湖五路各置鑄錢監，江西、湖南十五萬緡、餘路十萬緡為額，仍申熟錢斤重之限。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered the five circuits of Jingxi, Huainan, Liangzhe, Jiangxi, and Jinghu each to establish coin-casting mints—Jiangxi and Hunan at 150,000 strings quota, remaining circuits 100,000 strings—still setting limits on the weight per jin of mature coin.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court ordered mints in Jingxi, Huainan, Liangzhe, Jiangxi, and Jinghu circuits, with quotas of 150,000 strings for Jiangxi and Hunan and 100,000 for the rest, plus minimum weight standards for finished coin.

sentences.zh: 又以興國軍、睦衡舒鄂惠州既置監六，通舊十六監，水陸回遠，增提點之官。

translations.literal: Also, with six mints already established at Xingguo Army, Muzhou, Heng, Shu, E, and Huizhou, together with the old sixteen mints, water and land routes being distant and circuitous, supervisory officials were increased.
translations.idiomatic: Six new mints at Xingguo Army, Muzhou, Hengzhou, Shuzhou, Ezhou, and Huizhou joined the sixteen existing ones; because transport over land and water was long and arduous, additional supervisory posts were created.

sentences.zh: 時諸路大率務於增額：韶惠州永通、阜民監舊額八十萬，至七年，增三十萬，及折二凡五十萬；

translations.literal: At that time the various circuits mostly strove to increase quotas: Yongtong at Shaozhou and Huizhou and Fumin Mint—old quota 800,000; by the seventh year increased 300,000, and with value-two totaling 500,000;
translations.idiomatic: Circuits then competed to raise quotas: the Yongtong mint at Shaozhou and Huizhou and the Fumin mint had an original quota of eight hundred thousand strings; by year seven they added three hundred thousand, reaching five hundred thousand with value-two coin included;

sentences.zh: 後衛州黎陽監歲增折二凡五萬緡，西京阜財監歲增市易本錢凡十萬緡，興州濟眾監歲增七萬二千餘緡，陝西三銅錢監各歲增五萬緡。

translations.literal: Later Liyang Mint in Weizhou annually increased value-two by 50,000 strings total; Fucai Mint in the Western Capital annually increased Market Exchange capital by 100,000 strings; Jizhong Mint in Xing annually increased 72,000-plus strings; three copper coin mints in Shaanxi each annually increased 50,000 strings.
translations.idiomatic: Liyang mint in Weizhou later added fifty thousand strings of value-two coin yearly; Fucai mint in the Western Capital added one hundred thousand strings in Market Exchange principal; Jizhong mint in Xingzhou added more than seventy-two thousand; and each of Shaanxi's three copper mints added fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 而睦州則置神泉，徐州則置寶豐，梧州以鉛錫易得，萬州以多鐵礦，皆置監。

translations.literal: Muzhou then established Shenquan; Xuzhou established Baofeng; Wuzhou because lead and tin were easily obtained; Wanzhou because iron ore was abundant—all established mints.
translations.idiomatic: Shenquan mint was opened in Muzhou, Baofeng in Xuzhou, and mints in Wuzhou and Wanzhou as well—the former for easy access to lead and tin, the latter for abundant iron ore.

sentences.zh: 又詔秦鳳等路即鳳翔府斜穀置監，已而所鑄錢青銅夾錫，脆惡易毀，罷之。

translations.literal: Also ordered Qinfeng and other circuits to establish a mint at Xiegu in Fengxiang Prefecture; soon the coins cast were bronze mixed with tin, brittle and poor, easily destroyed—abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Qinfeng circuit was also told to open a mint at Xiegu in Fengxiang Prefecture, but the alloy—bronze adulterated with tin—proved brittle and was shut down.

sentences.zh: 然私錢往往雜用，不能禁，至是法弊，乃詔禁私錢，在官惡錢不堪用者，別為模以鑄。

translations.literal: Yet private coin was often mixed in use, impossible to prohibit; at this point the law failed; then an edict prohibited private coin; official bad coin unfit for use—separate molds were made to recast.
translations.idiomatic: Private coin continued to circulate in defiance of the ban. When the system broke down, the court outlawed private cash and ordered worn official coin reminted from new dies.

sentences.zh: 商、虢、洛南增三監，耀、鄜權置兩監，通永興、華、河中、陝舊監為九，以給改鑄。

translations.literal: Shang, Guo, and Luonan added three mints; Yao and Fu provisionally established two mints—together with old mints at Yongxing, Hua, Hezhong, and Shaan totaling nine—to supply recoining.
translations.idiomatic: Three new mints opened at Shangzhou, Guozhou, and Luonan, with two temporary ones at Yaozhou and Fuzhou, joining Yongxing, Hua, Hezhong, and Shaan prefectures' existing mints for nine in all, dedicated to recoining.

sentences.zh: 永興、鄜、耀、河中、陝去鐵冶遠，聽改鑄一年罷；

translations.literal: Yongxing, Fu, Yao, Hezhong, and Shaan were far from iron smelters—permitted to recoin for one year then cease;
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing, Fu, Yao, Hezhong, and Shaan prefectures, being far from ironworks, were allowed one year of recoining before closing;

sentences.zh: 商、洛南、華、虢最近鐵冶，聽久置；

translations.literal: Shang, Luonan, Hua, and Guo were nearest iron smelters—permitted long-term establishment;
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhou, Luonan, Hua, and Guozhou, nearest the ironworks, were permitted to remain open indefinitely;

sentences.zh: 鄜州等五監候罷改鑄，並其工作歸永興等四監，專鑄大錢，所鑄大鐵錢約補及所廢偽錢，及可以待交子所用而止。

translations.literal: The five mints including Fu Prefecture awaiting abolition after recoining—their labor combined into the four mints including Yongxing, exclusively casting large coins; large iron coins cast approximately to replace abolished counterfeit coin, and stop when sufficient for use with jiaozi [paper money].
translations.idiomatic: When recoining finished, the five mints including Fuzhou would close and merge into Yongxing and three others, which would mint large iron cash only until enough had been produced to replace withdrawn counterfeit coin and supply jiaozi redemption.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔河東鑄錢七十萬緡外，增鑄小錢三十萬緡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict [ordered that] beyond Hedong's 700,000 strings of coin casting, additionally cast 300,000 strings of small coins.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight, Hedong was told to mint an extra three hundred thousand strings of small coin beyond its base quota of seven hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 於是知太原韓絳請仿陝西令本重模精，以息私鑄之弊。

translations.literal: Thereupon Taiyuan prefect Han Jiang requested imitating Shaanxi, making the standard weight and dies precise, to quell the abuse of illicit casting.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan prefect Han Jiang then asked to follow Shaanxi's example of strict weight and fine dies to curb counterfeiting.

sentences.zh: 初，薛向鑄鐵錢於陝西，後許彥先鑄於廣南。

translations.literal: Initially Xue Xiang cast iron coins in Shaanxi; later Xu Yanxian cast in Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiang had first minted iron cash in Shaanxi; later Xu Yanxian did so in Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 既而民不便用，神宗欲遂罷之，王安石固爭，乃詔京師畿內並罷，其行於四方蓋如故。

translations.literal: Soon the people found it inconvenient to use; Emperor Shenzong wished to abolish it entirely; Wang Anshi firmly contested; then an edict abolished it in the capital metropolitan region together; its circulation in the four directions probably remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The public soon found iron cash unwieldy. Shenzong wanted to abolish it entirely, but Wang Anshi objected fiercely. Iron coin was withdrawn only from the capital region; elsewhere it continued much as before.

sentences.zh: 元豐以後，西師大舉，邊用匱闕，徐州置寶豐下監，歲鑄折二錢二十萬緡，轉移陝府。

translations.literal: After Yuanfeng, western armies were broadly deployed; frontier expenses were deficient; Baofeng sub-mint was established at Xuzhou, annually casting 200,000 strings of value-two coins, transferred to Shaan-fu [Shaanxi capital district].
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanfeng, with western campaigns in full swing and frontier funds depleted, a subsidiary Baofeng mint in Xuzhou coined two hundred thousand strings of value-two cash yearly for shipment to the Shaanxi capital.

sentences.zh: 於時，同、渭、秦、隴等州錢監，廢置移徙不一，銅鐵官多建言鑄錢，事不盡行，而又自弛錢禁，民之銷毀與夫闌出境外者為多。

translations.literal: At that time, coin mints in Tong, Wei, Qin, Long, and other prefectures—abolished, established, moved—not uniform; copper and iron officials often memorialized on casting coins, matters not all implemented; moreover they themselves relaxed coin prohibitions; the people's melting down and smuggling out beyond the borders were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Mints in Tong, Wei, Qin, Long, and other prefectures were opened, closed, and relocated erratically. Copper and iron officials constantly proposed new mints, few of which took effect, while coin controls were quietly relaxed. Melting and illicit export surged.

sentences.zh: 張方平嘗極諫曰：「禁銅造幣，盜鑄者抵罪至死，示不與天下共其利也。

translations.literal: Zhang Fangping once urgently remonstrated, saying: "Prohibiting copper to mint currency—illicit casters punished up to death—shows unwillingness to share profit with all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fangping once protested vehemently: "Monopolizing copper for coinage and punishing counterfeiters with death signals that the state will not share this profit with the realm.

sentences.zh: 故事，諸監所鑄錢悉入於王府，歲出其奇羨給之三司，方流布於天下。

translations.literal: By precedent, all coin cast at the various mints entered the imperial treasury; yearly its surplus was dispensed to the Bureau of Revenue, then only then circulated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, mint output went first to the imperial treasury; only the surplus passed each year to the Bureau of Revenue for release into circulation.

sentences.zh: 然自太祖平江南，江、池、饒、建置爐，歲鼓鑄至百萬緡。

translations.literal: Yet since Taizu pacified Jiangnan, Jiang, Chi, Rao, and Jian established furnaces; yearly hammer-casting reached one million strings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Taizu's conquest of Jiangnan, mints in Jiang, Chi, Rao, and Jian had poured out a million strings a year.

sentences.zh: 積百年所入，宜乎貫朽於中藏，充足於民間矣。

translations.literal: Accumulating a century of receipts—ought not strings rot in the central vaults and fill the populace?
translations.idiomatic: A century of such intake should have rotted strings in the central vaults and filled every purse in the land.

sentences.zh: 比年公私上下並苦乏錢，百貨不通，人情窘迫，謂之錢荒。

translations.literal: In recent years public and private, above and below, alike suffered coin shortage; all goods did not circulate; people's circumstances were straitened—called "coin famine."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent years everyone from the throne to the street has strained under scarcity; trade has stalled and hardship spread—the age of the "coin famine."

sentences.zh: 不知歲所鑄錢，今將安在。

translations.literal: One does not know where the yearly cast coin has gone today.
translations.idiomatic: Where has all the coin minted each year gone?

sentences.zh: 夫鑄錢禁銅之法舊矣，令敕具載，而自熙寧七年頒行新敕，刪去舊條，削除錢禁，以此邊關重車而出，海舶飽載而回，聞沿邊州軍錢出外界，但每貫收稅錢而已。

translations.literal: Now the laws on casting coin and prohibiting copper are old; orders and edicts fully record them; yet since the new edict issued in the seventh year of Xining deleted old articles and eliminated coin prohibitions—for this reason frontier passes see heavy carts depart; sea ships return fully laden; heard that along frontier prefectures and armies coin exits the outer realm, merely collecting tax per string.
translations.idiomatic: Laws governing minting and copper monopoly are ancient and fully codified, yet the Xining 7 edict struck the old clauses and gutted coin controls. Heavy carts now rumble through frontier passes; returning ships ride low with cargo. Coin flows abroad from border garrisons, taxed at a few coins per string and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 錢本中國寶貨，今乃與四夷共用，又自廢罷銅禁，民間銷毀無復可辦。

translations.literal: Coin is originally China's treasured commodity; now it is shared with the four barbarians; moreover copper prohibition was abolished on one's own—popular melting down can no longer be prevented.
translations.idiomatic: Coin is the empire's treasure, yet now barbarians use it freely. With copper controls lifted, nothing stops the people from melting it down.

sentences.zh: 銷鎔十錢得精銅一兩，造作器用，獲利五倍。

translations.literal: Smelting ten coins yields one liang of fine copper; making utensils—profit fivefold.
translations.idiomatic: Ten coins smelted yield one liang of pure copper; fashioned into vessels, the profit is fivefold.

sentences.zh: 如此則逐州置爐，每爐增數，是猶畎澮之益，而供尾閭之泄也。」

translations.literal: Thus establishing furnaces in each prefecture, each furnace increasing numbers—is like the benefit of irrigation ditches, yet supplying the outflow of the tail-lock."
translations.idiomatic: To open more mints in every prefecture and raise each quota is to pour water into ditches while the sluice at the end runs ever open."

sentences.zh: 元豐八年，哲宗嗣位，復申錢幣闌出之禁，如嘉祐編敕；

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanfeng, Emperor Zhezong succeeded; revived prohibition on smuggling coin out, as in the Jiayou compiled statutes;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanfeng, when Zhezong acceded, export controls on coin were restored as under the Jiayou code;

sentences.zh: 罷徐州寶豐鼓鑄；

translations.literal: abolished hammer-casting at Baofeng in Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: the Baofeng mint in Xuzhou was shut down;

sentences.zh: 詔戶部條諸監之可減者，凡增置鑄錢監十四皆罷之。

translations.literal: ordered the Ministry of Revenue to catalog mints that could be reduced; all fourteen additionally established coin mints were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: and the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to review reducible mints, closing all fourteen added since the expansion.

sentences.zh: 陝西行鐵錢，至陝府以東即銅錢地，民以鐵錢換易，有輕重不等之患。

translations.literal: Shaanxi circulated iron coins; east of Shaan-fu was copper coin territory; the people exchanged iron for copper—there was the trouble of unequal weight and value.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi used iron cash, but east of the Shaanxi capital lay copper-coin country, and exchange between the two bred inequalities of weight and value.

sentences.zh: 元祐六年，乃議限東行，有稅物者以十分率之，止許易二分，人毋得過五千。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanyou, then deliberated limiting eastward movement: those with taxable goods—calculate by tenths, only permit exchange of two parts; per person not exceeding five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 6, regulators proposed limiting eastward export: for goods assessed at ten parts, only two parts' worth might be exchanged, capped at five thousand per person.

sentences.zh: 八年，命公私給納、貿易並專用鐵錢，而官帑銅錢以時計置，運致內郡，商旅願於陝西內郡入便銅錢，給據請於別路者聽。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, ordered public and private payments and trade all exclusively to use iron coins; official copper coins to be calculated and set aside in season, transported to inner commanderies; merchants traveling who wished to deposit convenient copper cash in inner commanderies of Shaanxi—issuing receipts to redeem on other circuits was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight, public and private payments and trade in the region were ordered to use iron cash exclusively, while copper coin in the treasury was periodically allocated and shipped inland. Merchants who deposited copper cash in inland Shaanxi prefectures could obtain receipts redeemable in other circuits.

sentences.zh: 仍定加饒之數，每百緡，河東、京西加饒三千，在京、餘路四千。

translations.literal: Still fixed the premium amounts: per hundred strings, Hedong and Jingxi premium three thousand; in the capital and remaining circuits four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Premium rates were set: three thousand per hundred strings in Hedong and Jingxi, four thousand in the capital and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 先是，太祖時取唐飛錢故事，許民入錢京師，於諸州便換。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Taizu's time they took the Tang precedent of flying money, permitting people to deposit cash in the capital and conveniently exchange in various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Taizu had revived the Tang "flying money" system, allowing deposits in the capital to be drawn in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 其法：商人入錢左藏庫，先經三司投牒，乃輸於庫。

translations.literal: The method: merchants depositing cash at the Left Treasury—first submit a petition through the Bureau of Revenue, then pay into the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Under the rules, merchants paid into the Left Treasury only after filing with the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，置便錢務，令商人入錢詣務陳牒，即輦致左藏庫，給以券，仍敕諸州凡商人齎券至，當日給付，違者科罰。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao, established the Convenient Cash Office; ordered merchants depositing cash to go to the office and present petitions; immediately carted to the Left Treasury, issued certificates; still commanded all prefectures that when merchants bearing certificates arrive, pay same day; violators punished.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 3 the Convenient Cash Office was created so merchants could deposit there, have funds transferred to the Left Treasury, and receive vouchers mandating same-day payout in any prefecture on pain of penalty.

sentences.zh: 至道末，商人入便錢一百七十餘萬貫，天禧末，增一百一十三萬貫。

translations.literal: End of Zhidao, merchants' convenient cash deposits 1.7-plus million guan; end of Tianxi, increased 1.13 million guan.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Zhidao, merchants had deposited more than 1.7 million guan; by Tianxi the figure had risen another 1.13 million.

sentences.zh: 至是，乃復增定加饒之數行焉。

translations.literal: At this time, then restored fixing premium amounts to implement them.
translations.idiomatic: The premium rates were now restored and put into effect.

sentences.zh: 折二銅錢又定鉤致之法。

translations.literal: Value-two copper coins again had a method fixed for gathering them back.
translations.idiomatic: Rules were also set for recalling value-two copper coin.

sentences.zh: 初欲復舊，止行於本路。

translations.literal: Initially wished to restore the old, circulating only within the home circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At first the plan was to revert to older coin, circulating only within each circuit.

sentences.zh: 議者謂：「關東諸路既已通行，奪彼予此，理亦非便。

translations.literal: Deliberators said: "East-of-Pass circuits already circulate them universally; taking from those and giving to these—in principle also not convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued: "East-of-Pass circuits already use this coin widely. Stripping one region to supply another makes little sense.

sentences.zh: 且陝右所用折二鐵錢，止當一小銅錢，即折二銅錢盡歸陝西，不直般運費廣，猝難鉤致，且與鐵錢一等，慮鐵錢轉更加輕。」

translations.literal: Moreover the value-two iron coins used in western Shaanxi are worth only one small copper coin; if value-two copper coins all return to Shaanxi, not worth the broad transport costs, suddenly hard to gather back; moreover equal with iron coins—fearing iron coins would grow even lighter."
translations.idiomatic: In western Shaanxi, value-two iron cash is worth only one small copper coin. Shipping all value-two copper there would cost more than it is worth and be hard to enforce. Treating copper and iron alike would only further debase iron cash."

sentences.zh: 乃令折二銅錢寬所行地，聽行於陝西一路，及河東晉、絳、石、慈、隰州，京西西京、河陽、許、汝、鄭、金、房、均、鄧等州，餘路則禁。

translations.literal: Then ordered value-two copper coins to broaden circulation territory—permitted in Shaanxi Circuit, and in Hedong's Jin, Jiang, Shi, Ci, and Xi Prefectures, Jingxi's Western Capital, Heyang, Xu, Ru, Zheng, Jin, Fang, Jun, Deng and other prefectures; remaining circuits prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Value-two copper was therefore allowed in Shaanxi circuit; Jin, Jiang, Shi, Ci, and Xi in Hedong; and Western Capital, Heyang, Xu, Ru, Zheng, Jin, Fang, Jun, and Deng in Jingxi—while other circuits were barred.

sentences.zh: 仍限二年毋更用，在民間者聽以輸買納，在官帑者以輸上供，即非沿流地或素無上供者，所隸運司移發輸京師。

translations.literal: Still limited to two years without further use; those among the populace permitted to use for tax payments and purchases; those in official treasuries to submit as tribute/supplies; if not along-stream territory or normally without tribute, the subordinate transport commission moved and dispatched to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Use was limited to two more years. Coin held by the public could be paid in taxes; coin in government stores would be sent as tribute, or forwarded to the capital by the local transport commission where tribute routes did not apply.

sentences.zh: 尋詔更鑄小銅錢。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered recasting small copper coins.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon ordered new small copper coin minted.

sentences.zh: 河東安撫、提刑司言：「頃絳州垣曲縣置監鼓鑄銅錢，費且不給，今已廢監，又禁折二銅錢不通行，非便。」

translations.literal: Hedong pacification and judicial inspection commissions said: "Recently Jiang Prefecture's Yuanqu County established a mint for hammer-casting copper coins—costs and couldn't supply; now the mint is abolished, yet value-two copper coins are prohibited from circulation—not convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Hedong's pacification and judicial commissions reported: "A mint at Yuanqu in Jiangzhou recently cost more than it produced and has closed. Banning value-two copper there is impractical."

sentences.zh: 乃聽行使如舊。

translations.literal: Then permitted circulation as before.
translations.idiomatic: Circulation was allowed to continue as before.

sentences.zh: 供備庫使鄭價使契丹還，言其給輿箱者錢，皆中國所鑄。

translations.literal: Palace Provision Store envoy Zheng Jia, returning from mission to Khitan, said those who supplied litters and boxes with cash—all were cast by China.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jia of the Palace Provision Store, returning from a Khitan mission, reported that cash paid for carts and carriers was all Chinese coin.

sentences.zh: 乃增嚴三路闌出之法。

translations.literal: Then increased strictness of smuggling prohibition on the three circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Export prohibitions on the three frontier circuits were tightened.

sentences.zh: 熙、豐間銅鐵錢嘗並行，銅錢千易鐵錢千五百，未聞輕重之弊。

translations.literal: Between Xi and Feng eras copper and iron coins once circulated together; one thousand copper exchanged for 1,500 iron—no reports of light/heavy abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xi and Feng, copper and iron coin had circulated side by side at one thousand copper to fifteen hundred iron, without reported debasement.

sentences.zh: 及後銅錢日少，鐵錢滋多。

translations.literal: Later copper coins daily fewer, iron coins increasingly many.
translations.idiomatic: Later copper grew scarce while iron multiplied.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，銅錢千遂易鐵錢二千五百，鐵錢浸輕。

translations.literal: Early in Shaosheng, one thousand copper coins then exchanged for 2,500 iron—iron coins gradually lighter.
translations.idiomatic: By early Shaosheng, one thousand copper fetched twenty-five hundred iron, and iron cash kept losing value.

sentences.zh: 元符二年，下陝西諸路安撫司博究利害。

translations.literal: Second year of Yuanfu, sent down to Shaanxi various circuits' pacification commissions to broadly investigate harms and benefits.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 2, Shaanxi circuit pacification offices were ordered to study the problem in depth.

sentences.zh: 於是詔陝西悉禁銅錢，在民間者令盡送官，而官銅悉取就京西置監。

translations.literal: Thereupon edict ordered Shaanxi entirely to prohibit copper coins; those among the populace ordered all sent to government; official copper all taken to establish mints in Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: The court then banned copper cash entirely in Shaanxi, ordered private holdings surrendered, and moved all official copper to new mints in Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 永興帥臣陸師閔言：「既揀毀私錢，禁銅罷冶，則物價當減。

translations.literal: Yongxing commander Lu Shimin said: "Having sorted and destroyed private coin, prohibited copper and stopped smelting—then goods prices ought to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing commander Lu Shimin argued: "Once private coin is culled and copper mining halted, prices should fall.

sentences.zh: 願下陝西州縣，凡有市買，並準度銅錢之直，以平其價。」

translations.literal: [He] wished to send down to Shaanxi prefectures and counties: for all market purchases, all measure by the value of copper coins, to level prices."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Shaanxi's prefectures and counties peg all market transactions to copper coin values to stabilize prices.

sentences.zh: 詔用其言，而豪賈蓄家多不便。

translations.literal: The edict adopted his words, but powerful merchants and hoarding households mostly found it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his proposal, but wealthy traders and hoarders found it burdensome.

sentences.zh: 徽宗嗣位，通判鳳州馬景夷言：「 陝西自去年罷使銅錢，續追官措置錢法，未聞有深究錢幣輕重灼見利害者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong succeeded, Feng Prefecture vice-prefect Ma Jingyi said: " Shaanxi since last year stopped using copper coins; subsequently officials pursued coinage measures, yet none have heard of anyone deeply investigating the lightness and heaviness of coin with clear sight of harms and benefits.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong acceded, Ma Jingyi, vice-prefect of Fengzhou, argued: "Since Shaanxi stopped using copper cash last year, officials have repeatedly adjusted coin policy, yet no one has thoroughly examined relative coin values and their real costs.

sentences.zh: 銅錢流注天下，雖千百年未嘗有輕重之患。

translations.literal: Copper coins flowed throughout the realm; though a thousand or a hundred years, never had the trouble of light and heavy [debasement].
translations.idiomatic: Copper coin had circulated empire-wide for centuries without debasement problems.

sentences.zh: 獨鐵錢局於一路，所可通交易有無者，限以十州之地，欲無滯礙，安可得乎？

translations.literal: Only iron coins confined to one circuit—those who could freely trade supply and demand—limited to the territory of ten prefectures; wishing for no obstruction, how could it be obtained?
