translations.idiomatic: Iron cash alone, confined to one circuit and roughly ten prefectures, cannot circulate freely. How can trade proceed without friction?

sentences.zh: 又諸州錢監鼓鑄不已，歲月增多，以鼓鑄無窮之錢，而供流轉有限之用，更數十年，積滯一隅，暴如丘山，公私為害，又倍於今日矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the various prefectures' coin mints hammer-cast without cease, increasing month by month; with endlessly cast coin to supply limited circulation—in several more decades, accumulation stagnating in one corner, piled like hills, public and private harmed, again double today's.
translations.idiomatic: Mints across the prefectures keep pouring out coin without pause. Coining without limit for limited circulation will, within decades, pile surpluses mountain-high in one region, harming public and private interests far worse than today.

sentences.zh: 謂宜弛其禁界，許鄰近陝西、河東等路特不入京城外，凡解鹽地州縣並許通行折二鐵錢。

translations.literal: [He] said it was fitting to relax the prohibition boundaries, permitting neighboring Shaanxi, Hedong, and other circuits—except not entering the capital city—to all salt-distribution prefectures and counties to permit circulation of value-two iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed easing border restrictions so value-two iron cash could circulate in Shaanxi, Hedong, and neighboring circuits—everywhere except the capital—and in all salt-distribution counties.

sentences.zh: 如此則流注無窮，久遠自無輕重之患。」

translations.literal: Thus then flow would be limitless; over the long term naturally no trouble of light and heavy."
translations.idiomatic: That would allow unbounded circulation and prevent debasement in the long run."

sentences.zh: 繼而言者謂：「鐵錢重滯，難以齎遠，民間皆願復用銅錢。

translations.literal: Subsequently speakers said: "Iron coins are heavy and sluggish, hard to carry far; among the people all wish to restore use of copper coins.
translations.idiomatic: Others added: "Iron cash is too heavy to transport, and the people want copper restored.

sentences.zh: 當公私匱乏之時，諸路州縣官私銅錢積貯萬數，反無所用。」

translations.literal: When public and private were depleted, various circuits' prefectures and counties, official and private copper coins accumulated in tens of thousands, yet had no use."
translations.idiomatic: Yet at a time of public and private scarcity, circuits were sitting on enormous hoards of copper cash that went unused."

sentences.zh: 乃詔銅鐵錢聽民間通行，而銅錢止用糴買。

translations.literal: Then an edict permitted copper and iron coins to circulate among the people, while copper coins were only used for grain purchases.
translations.idiomatic: The court then allowed both metals to circulate, but restricted copper coin to grain purchases.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國元年，陝西轉運副使孫傑以鐵錢多而銅錢少，請復鑄銅錢，候銅鐵錢輕重稍均，即聽兼鑄。

translations.literal: First year of Jianzhong Jingguo, Shaanxi vice transport commissioner Sun Jie, because iron coins were many and copper coins few, requested restoring copper coin casting; when copper and iron coin lightness and heaviness were somewhat equal, then permit concurrent casting.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong Jingguo 1, Shaanxi vice transport commissioner Sun Jie, noting too much iron and too little copper, asked to resume copper minting and permit dual minting once values balanced.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，前陝西轉運判官都貺復請權罷陝西鑄鐵錢。

translations.literal: First year of Chongning, former Shaanxi transport aide Du Chang again requested provisionally stopping Shaanxi iron coin casting.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 1, former Shaanxi transport aide Du Chang asked to suspend iron minting in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書吳居厚言：「江、池、饒、建錢額不敷，議減銅增鉛、錫，歲可省銅三十餘萬斤，計增鑄錢十五萬九千餘緡。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Wu Juhou said: "Jiang, Chi, Rao, and Jian coin quotas did not meet targets; deliberated reducing copper and increasing lead and tin—yearly could save over 300,000 jin of copper, calculating increased casting of 159,000-plus strings.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Minister Wu Juhou reported: "Jiang, Chi, Rao, and Jian mints miss their quotas. Adding lead and tin while reducing copper could save over three hundred thousand jin of copper yearly and add more than 159,000 strings of output.

sentences.zh: 所鑄光明堅韌，與見行錢不異。」

translations.literal: What was cast was bright, firm, and tough—no different from currently circulating coin."
translations.idiomatic: The new alloy would be bright and durable, indistinguishable from existing coin."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 然課猶不登。

translations.literal: Yet quotas still were not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Quotas remained unmet, however.

sentences.zh: 二年，居厚乃請檢用前後上供鑄錢條約，視其登耗之數，別定勸沮之法。

translations.literal: Second year, Juhou then requested examining and applying prior and subsequent tribute coin-casting regulations, viewing surplus and deficit numbers, separately fixing methods of encouragement and deterrence.
translations.idiomatic: In year two, Juhou asked to enforce tribute minting rules with rewards and penalties based on shortfalls and surpluses.

sentences.zh: 會蔡京當政，將以利惑人主，托假紹述，肆為紛更。

translations.literal: As Cai Jing held power, he intended to beguile the sovereign with profit, borrowing the pretext of reviving [prior policies], wantonly making chaotic changes.
translations.idiomatic: With Cai Jing in power, he sought to dazzle the throne with profit, invoking a return to earlier policies while pushing radical changes.

sentences.zh: 有許天啟者，京之黨也，時為陝西轉運副使，迎合京意，請鑄當十錢。

translations.literal: There was one Xu Tianqi—Cai's faction member—at that time Shaanxi vice transport commissioner, catering to Cai's intent, requesting casting value-ten coins.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tianqi, a Cai partisan serving as Shaanxi vice transport commissioner, proposed value-ten coin to please his patron.

sentences.zh: 五月，始令陝西及江、池、饒、建州，以歲所鑄小平錢增料改鑄當五大銅錢，以「聖宋通寶」為文，繼而並令舒、睦、衡、鄂錢監，用陝西式鑄折十錢，限今歲鑄三十萬緡，鐵錢二百萬緡。

translations.literal: Fifth month, first ordered Shaanxi and Jiang, Chi, Rao, and Jian Prefectures, using yearly cast small coins with added material to recast as value-five large copper coins, with "Sheng Song Tongbao" as inscription; subsequently also ordered Shu, Mu, Heng, and E mints, using Shaanxi-style to cast value-ten coins, limiting this year to cast 300,000 strings, iron coins 2 million strings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Shaanxi and Jiang, Chi, Rao, and Jian were told to recast small coin into value-five copper bearing "Sheng Song Universal Treasure." Shu, Mu, Heng, and E mints soon followed with Shaanxi-style value-ten coin, capped at three hundred thousand strings of copper and two million of iron for the year.

sentences.zh: 募私鑄人丁為官匠，並其家設營以居之，號鑄錢院，謂得昔人招天下亡命即山鑄錢之意。

translations.literal: Recruited illicit casters as official artisans, also establishing camps for their families to dwell, called Coin-Casting Court—claiming to obtain the ancient intent of recruiting fugitives from all under Heaven to cast coin at mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiters were recruited as official artisans, with camps housing their families—the "Coin-Casting Court"—invoking the old practice of enlisting fugitive minters.

sentences.zh: 所鑄銅錢通行諸路，而陝西、河東、四川係鐵錢地者禁之，第鑄於陝西鐵錢地而已。

translations.literal: Copper coins cast circulated in various circuits, while Shaanxi, Hedong, and Sichuan—iron coin territories—were prohibited; only cast in Shaanxi iron-coin territory.
translations.idiomatic: The new copper circulated across circuits but was barred from Shaanxi, Hedong, and Sichuan iron-coin zones; iron coin was minted only within Shaanxi's iron region.

sentences.zh: 自熙寧以來，折二錢雖行民間，法不許運致京師，故諸州所積甚多。

translations.literal: Since Xining, value-two coins though circulated among the people, the law did not permit transport to the capital, so various prefectures accumulated greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xining, value-two coin had circulated locally but could not be shipped to the capital, so prefectures had amassed huge stocks.

sentences.zh: 至是，發運司因請以官帑所有折二錢改鑄折十錢。

translations.literal: At this time, the Transport Commission therefore requested using official treasuries' value-two coins to recast as value-ten coins.
translations.idiomatic: The Transport Commission then proposed recoining official stocks of value-two cash into value-ten.

sentences.zh: 三年，遂罷鑄小平錢及折五錢。

translations.literal: Third year, then abolished casting small coins and value-five coins.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, minting of small coin and value-five coin ceased.

sentences.zh: 置監於京城所，復徐州寶豐、衛州黎陽監，並改鑄折二錢為折十，舊折二錢期一歲勿用。

translations.literal: Established mints at the Capital Office, restored Baofeng in Xuzhou and Liyang in Weizhou mints, all recasting value-two coins as value-ten; old value-two coins given one year then not to be used.
translations.idiomatic: Mints were opened at the capital office and Baofeng and Liyang restored, all recoining value-two into value-ten; old value-two coin had one year before withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 大嚴私鑄之令，民間所用鍮石器物，並官造鬻之，輒鑄者依私有法加二等。

translations.literal: Greatly tightened illicit-casting orders; brass vessels used among the people—all government-made and sold; those who cast anyway—under private-property law increase two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiting laws were tightened sharply. Brass utensils used by commoners were sold only by the state, and illegal casting drew penalties two degrees harsher than ordinary theft.

sentences.zh: 命諸路轉運司於沿流順便地，隨宜增置錢監，俾民以所有折二錢換納於官，運致所增監改鑄折十錢。

translations.literal: Ordered various circuits' transport commissions at convenient riverside locations as appropriate to add mints, enabling people to exchange value-two coins they held to government, transported to added mints to recast as value-ten coins.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissions were told to add mints along convenient waterways, accept value-two coin from the public, and recoin it as value-ten at the new facilities.

sentences.zh: 二廣產鐵，令鼓鑄小鐵錢，止行於兩路；

translations.literal: Liang Guang produced iron; ordered hammer-casting small iron coins, only circulating within the two circuits;
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong and Guangxi, rich in iron, were ordered to mint small iron cash for local use only;

sentences.zh: 其公私銅錢兌換運輸元豐庫，仍於潯州置鐵錢監，依陝西料例鑄當二錢。

translations.literal: Public and private copper coins exchanged and transported to Yuanfeng Treasury; still established iron coin mint at Xun Prefecture, following Shaanxi material standards to cast value-two coins.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private copper was exchanged and sent to the Yuanfeng treasury, and an iron mint opened at Xunzhou casting value-two coin on the Shaanxi model.

sentences.zh: 四年，立錢綱驗樣法。

translations.literal: Fourth year, established coin-convoy sample-inspection law.
translations.idiomatic: In year four, regulations were set for inspecting coin convoy samples.

sentences.zh: 崇寧監以所鑄御書當十錢來上，緡用銅九斤七兩有奇，鉛半之，錫居三之一。

translations.literal: Chongning Mint presented the imperial-script value-ten coins cast—per string used copper nine jin seven liang and a fraction, lead half that, tin one-third.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongning mint submitted sample value-ten coin with imperial calligraphy: nine jin seven liang plus of copper per string, half as much lead, and tin one-third of the remainder.

sentences.zh: 詔頒其式於諸路，令赤仄烏背，書畫分明。

translations.literal: Edict promulgated its model to various circuits, ordering reddish oblique edge and black back, inscription and design clear.
translations.idiomatic: The formula was issued empire-wide: reddish clipped edge, dark back, and crisp lettering.

sentences.zh: 時趙挺之為門下侍郎，繼拜右僕射，與蔡京議多不合，因極言當十錢不便，私鑄浸廣。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Tingzhi was Gate Gentleman attendant, subsequently appointed Right Vice Director; disagreed much with Cai Jing on deliberations, therefore urgently spoke that value-ten coins were inconvenient, illicit casting gradually broad.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingzhi, recently promoted from vice director of the Secretariat to right vice director, clashed with Cai Jing and warned that value-ten coin was impractical and counterfeiting was spreading.

sentences.zh: 乃令提刑司歲較巡捕官一路所獲多寡，繼令福建、廣南毋行用，第鑄以上供及給他路。

translations.literal: Then ordered judicial inspection commissions yearly to compare patrol officers' captures per circuit; subsequently ordered Fujian and Guangnan not to circulate, only cast for tribute and supply to other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial commissions were told to rank circuit officers by seizures yearly. Fujian and Guangnan were barred from using value-ten coin locally; they minted only for tribute and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 凡為人附帶若封識影庇私鑄錢者，悉論以法，毋得蔭贖。

translations.literal: All who for others carried or sealed and sheltered illicit cast coin—all judged by law, not permitted commutation.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone carrying, concealing, or shielding counterfeit coin faced full prosecution without commutation.

sentences.zh: 其置鑄錢院，蓋將以盡收所在亡命盜鑄之人，然犯法者不為止。

translations.literal: Establishing the Coin-Casting Court—intended to fully gather local fugitive illicit casters; yet lawbreakers did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Coin-Casting Court was meant to absorb fugitive counterfeiters, yet crime did not stop.

sentences.zh: 乃命荊湖南北、江南東西、兩浙並以折十錢為折五，舊折二錢仍舊。

translations.literal: Then ordered Jinghu South and North, Jiangnan East and West, Liangzhe—all value-ten coins became value-five; old value-two coins remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Value-ten coin was revalued to value-five in Jinghu, Jiangnan, and Liangzhe circuits, while old value-two coin continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 慮冒法入東北也，今以江為界，淮南重寶錢亦作當五用焉。

translations.literal: Fearing illegal entry into the Northeast; now taking the Yangzi as boundary; Huainan heavy treasure coins also made for value-five use.
translations.idiomatic: To prevent illicit export to the northeast, the Yangzi was set as the boundary, and Huainan's heavy treasure coin was also rated at value-five.

sentences.zh: 五年，兩浙盜鑄尤甚，小平錢益少，市易濡滯。

translations.literal: Fifth year, Liangzhe illicit casting especially severe, small coins increasingly few, market trade sluggish.
translations.idiomatic: In year five, counterfeiting was worst in Liangzhe; small coin grew scarce and trade stalled.

sentences.zh: 遂命以折五、折十上供，小平錢留本路；

translations.literal: Then ordered value-five and value-ten for tribute, small coins retained in home circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Value-five and value-ten were ordered sent as tribute while small coin stayed in each circuit.

sentences.zh: 江、池、饒、建、韶州錢監，歲課以八分鑄小平錢，二分鑄當十錢。

translations.literal: Jiang, Chi, Rao, Jian, and Shao mints—yearly quota: eight parts cast small coins, two parts cast value-ten coins.
translations.idiomatic: Mint quotas in Jiang, Chi, Rao, Jian, and Shao were set at eighty percent small coin and twenty percent value-ten.

sentences.zh: 俄詔廣南、江南、福建、兩浙、荊湖、淮南用折二錢改鑄折十錢皆罷，其創置鑄錢院及招置錢戶並停。

translations.literal: Soon edict: Guangnan, Jiangnan, Fujian, Liangzhe, Jinghu, Huainan—all using value-two coins to recast value-ten coins abolished; newly established Coin-Casting Courts and recruited coin households all stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Recoining value-two into value-ten was halted in Guangnan, Jiangnan, Fujian, Liangzhe, Jinghu, and Huainan, and all new mint complexes and recruited households were shut down.

sentences.zh: 繼復罷鑄當十二分之令，盡鑄小平錢。

translations.literal: Subsequently again abolished the order to cast two parts in ten as value-ten, entirely casting small coins.
translations.idiomatic: The two-tenths value-ten casting quota was dropped and mints returned to small coin only.

sentences.zh: 荊湖、江南、兩浙、淮南重寶錢作當三，在京、京畿、京東西、河東、河北、陝西、熙河作當五。

translations.literal: Jinghu, Jiangnan, Liangzhe, Huainan heavy treasure coins made value-three; in capital, capital metropolitan region, Jingdong and Jingxi, Hedong, Hebei, Shaanxi, Xihe made value-five.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy treasure coin was rated value-three in Jinghu, Jiangnan, Liangzhe, and Huainan, and value-five in the capital region, Jingdong, Jingxi, Hedong, Hebei, Shaanxi, and Xihe.

sentences.zh: 通寶錢所鑄未多，在官者悉封樁，在民間者以小平錢納換。

translations.literal: Tongbao coins cast were not many; those in government all sealed in store; those among the people exchanged with small coins.
translations.idiomatic: Relatively little Sheng Song Tongbao had been minted. Official stocks were sealed, and private holdings were bought back with small coin.

sentences.zh: 旋復詔京畿、京東西、河北、河東、陝西、熙河當十錢仍舊，兩浙作當三，江南、淮南、荊湖作當五。

translations.literal: Soon again edict: capital metropolitan region, Jingdong and Jingxi, Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, Xihe—value-ten coins remained as before; Liangzhe made value-three; Jiangnan, Huainan, Jinghu made value-five.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the capital region, Jingdong, Jingxi, Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, and Xihe kept value-ten coin; Liangzhe used value-three; Jiangnan, Huainan, and Jinghu value-five.

sentences.zh: 時錢幣苦重，條序不一，私鑄日甚。

translations.literal: At that time coin types painfully heavy, regulations not uniform, illicit casting daily more severe.
translations.idiomatic: Denominations had become unwieldy, rules conflicting, and counterfeiting daily worse.

sentences.zh: 御史沈畸奏曰：「小錢便民久矣。

translations.literal: Censor Shen Ji memorialized, saying: "Small coins have long been convenient for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shen Ji wrote: "Small coin has served the people well for ages.

sentences.zh: 古者軍興，錫賞不繼，或以一當百，或以一當千。

translations.literal: Anciently when armies rose, bestowing rewards could not continue, sometimes one for a hundred, sometimes one for a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, during war when pay ran short, coins were debased to one-for-a-hundred or one-for-a-thousand.

sentences.zh: 此權時之宜，豈可行於太平無事之日哉？

translations.literal: This was expedient for the moment—how could it be practiced in days of peace without incident?
translations.idiomatic: That was a wartime expedient—not policy for peacetime.

sentences.zh: 當十鼓鑄，有數倍之息，雖日漸之，其勢不可遏。」

translations.literal: Value-ten hammer-casting had several-fold profit; though gradually [reduced], its momentum could not be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Value-ten minting yielded several times the profit; even gradual debasement could not check the tide."

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔當十錢止行於京師、陝西、河東、河北。

translations.literal: Before long, edict: value-ten coins only circulated in the capital, Shaanxi, Hedong, and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Value-ten coin was soon restricted to the capital, Shaanxi, Hedong, and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 俄並畿內用之，餘路悉禁。

translations.literal: Soon also permitted in metropolitan inner region; all remaining circuits entirely prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: The capital environs were included shortly after; all other circuits were barred.

sentences.zh: 期一季送官，償以小錢，換納到者輸於元豐、崇寧庫，而私錢亦限一季自致，計銅直增二分，償以小錢，隱藏者論如法。

translations.literal: Fixed one season to send to government, compensated with small coins; exchanged and paid in delivered to Yuanfeng and Chongning treasuries; private coin also limited one season to deliver oneself, calculating copper value increase two parts, compensated with small coins; those hiding—judged by law.
translations.idiomatic: Holders had one quarter to surrender value-ten coin for small coin at the Yuanfeng and Chongning treasuries. Private coin could also be turned in within a quarter at copper value plus two percent in small coin; concealment brought prosecution.

sentences.zh: 尋詔鄭州、西京亦聽用折十錢，禁貿易為二價者。

translations.literal: Soon edict: Zheng and Western Capital also permitted to use value-ten coins; prohibited trade at two prices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhou and the Western Capital were soon added; dual pricing was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 東南諸監增鑄小平錢，以待償錢，而私錢亦改鑄焉。

translations.literal: Southeast various mints increased casting small coins, to await compensation coin; private coin also recast.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast mints ramped up small coin production for buybacks, and private coin was recoined as well.

sentences.zh: 折十錢為幣既重，一旦更令，則民驟失厚利。

translations.literal: Value-ten coins as currency being already heavy [denomination], once orders changed, the people suddenly lost thick profit.
translations.idiomatic: Value-ten coin had become a lucrative denomination; the policy reversal suddenly stripped the public of those gains.

sentences.zh: 又諸路或用或否，往往不盡輸於官，冒法私販。

translations.literal: Moreover various circuits—some used, some not—often did not fully deliver to government, defying law in private trafficking.
translations.idiomatic: Some circuits still used value-ten coin, others did not, and many withheld holdings for illicit trade.

sentences.zh: 始令四輔、畿內、開封府許搜索舟車，賞視舊法增倍。

translations.literal: First ordered Four Adjuncts, metropolitan inner region, and Kaifeng Prefecture permitted to search boats and carts; rewards compared with old law doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in the Four Adjuncts, capital environs, and Kaifeng were authorized to search boats and carts, with rewards doubled from prior law.

sentences.zh: 水陸所由，官司失察者皆停替，而受納不揀選、容私錢其間者，以差定罪法。

translations.literal: Water and land route keepers—official offices failing inspection all suspended and replaced; those receiving payments without sorting and screening, permitting private coin among them—sentenced by degrees under law.
translations.idiomatic: Route officials who failed inspections were removed. Accepting payment without screening for private coin drew graded penalties.

sentences.zh: 又以私錢猥多，不能悉禁，乃令外路每一私錢，計小平錢三，以小錢易於官，在京以四小平錢易之。

translations.literal: Also because private coin was excessively many, could not entirely prohibit; then ordered outer circuits every one private coin, counted as three small coins, exchange small coins at government; in capital with four small coins exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Private coin was too abundant to ban outright, so the court offered exchange: three small coins per private coin in the provinces, four in the capital.

sentences.zh: 京師出納及民間貿易，並大小錢參用，而私鑄小平錢輒行用。

translations.literal: Capital receipts and disbursements and popular trade—all large and small coins mixed in use; illicitly cast small coins promptly circulated.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, official payments and private trade mixed large and small coin, and counterfeit small coin circulated freely.

sentences.zh: 立搜索告捕罪賞，越江、淮入汴錢至京者，一依當十錢法。

translations.literal: Established search, report, and capture crime rewards; crossing Yangzi and Huai into Bian—coin reaching the capital—all follow value-ten coin law.
translations.idiomatic: Search-and-report rewards were instituted. Coin brought from beyond the Yangzi and Huai to the capital faced the same value-ten rules.

sentences.zh: 御史張茂直請嚴私販當十之令，綱舟載卸，皆選官監索，保無藏匿，舟車兜擔，即疑慮私販者，並聽搜索；

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Maozhi requested strictening private trafficking of value-ten orders; convoy boats loading and unloading—all select officials to supervise search, guarantee no concealment; boat and cart porters—immediately suspecting private trafficking—all permitted search;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Maozhi urged stricter anti-smuggling rules: convoy boats were to be searched under appointed officers, and porters on boats and carts suspected of smuggling could be searched on sight.

sentences.zh: 而福建民或私鑄轉入淮、浙、京東等路者，所由州縣官司皆治漏逸之罪，不以赦免。

translations.literal: Whereas Fujian people sometimes illicitly cast and transferred into Huai, Zhe, Jingdong and other circuits—the responsible prefectures and counties' offices all punished leakage offenses, not exempted by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian counterfeiters who moved coin into Huai, Zhe, and Jingdong circuits were prosecuted for smuggling without amnesty.

sentences.zh: 法滋密矣。

translations.literal: The laws grew ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: The legal net tightened further.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，張茂直復言：「州縣督捕加峻，私小黃錢投委江河，不敢復出。

translations.literal: First year of Daguan, Zhang Maozhi again said: "Prefectures and counties' supervision and capture grew severe; private small yellow coins were thrown into rivers, not daring to come out again.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 1, Zhang Maozhi reported: "Harsh enforcement has driven holders to dump private small coin into rivers rather than risk detection.

sentences.zh: 請令東南州縣置水匱封鍵於闤闠中，聽民以私錢自投，如自首法。

translations.literal: Requested ordering Southeast prefectures and counties to place sealed water chests in marketplaces, permitting people to voluntarily deposit private coin, as under self-confession law.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that sealed chests be placed in market squares across the southeast so people could surrender private coin as under amnesty law.

sentences.zh: 當三、當五錢，舟船附帶者，亦多棄之江河，請下諸路撈漉。」

translations.literal: Value-three and value-five coins—those carried on boats—also mostly abandoned in rivers; requested sending down to various circuits to dredge and scoop."
translations.idiomatic: Value-three and value-five coin was also being thrown overboard. He urged circuits to dredge rivers for recovered coin."

sentences.zh: 時蔡京復相，再主用折十錢。

translations.literal: At that time Cai Jing again became chief minister, again taking the lead in using value-ten coins.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing had returned as chief minister and again pushed value-ten coin.

sentences.zh: 二月，首鑄御書當十錢，以京畿錢監所得私錢改鑄。

translations.literal: Second month, first cast imperial-script value-ten coins, using metropolitan mints' obtained private coin to recast.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, imperial-script value-ten coin was minted first from private coin seized at capital mints.

sentences.zh: 尋興復京畿兩監，以轉運使宋喬年領之，用提舉京畿鑄錢司為名。

translations.literal: Soon revived two metropolitan mints, with transport commissioner Song Qiaonian overseeing, using the name Office for Supervising Metropolitan Coin Casting.
translations.idiomatic: Two capital mints were reopened under transport commissioner Song Qiaonian as the Metropolitan Coin-Casting Supervisory Office.

sentences.zh: 喬年鑄烏背漉銅錢來上，詔以漉銅式頒行諸路。

translations.literal: Qiaonian cast black-back filtered-copper coins and presented them; edict promulgated the filtered-copper model to various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiaonian submitted black-back filtered-copper coin, and the alloy formula was issued empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 京之初為折十錢，人不以為便，帝亦知之。

translations.literal: When Jing first made value-ten coins, people did not find them convenient; the Emperor also knew this.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing's original value-ten coin had never pleased the public, and the emperor knew it.

sentences.zh: 故崇寧四年以後，稍更其法，及京去位，遂詔諭中外。

translations.literal: Therefore after Chongning fourth year, slightly changed its law; when Jing left office, then edict announced to inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongning 4 the rules were gradually revised, and when Cai fell from power an edict addressed the empire.

sentences.zh: 京再得政復行之，知盜鑄者必眾，將威以刑。

translations.literal: Jing again gained power and restored it; knowing illicit casters would surely be numerous, intended to awe with punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to power, Cai revived value-ten coin, expecting widespread counterfeiting and intending to crush it by force.

sentences.zh: 會有告蘇州章綖盜鑄數千萬緡，遂興大獄。

translations.literal: There happened a report that Suzhou's Zhang Tuan illicitly cast tens of millions of strings; then raised a great case.
translations.idiomatic: A tip that Zhang Tuan of Suzhou had counterfeited tens of millions of strings sparked a major prosecution.

sentences.zh: 初遣李孝壽，又遣沈畸、蕭服，末以命知蘇州孫傑、發運副使吳擇仁。

translations.literal: First sent Li Xiaoshou, then sent Shen Ji and Xiao Fu, finally entrusted to Suzhou prefect Sun Jie and transport vice commissioner Wu Zeren.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoshou was sent first, then Shen Ji and Xiao Fu, and finally Suzhou prefect Sun Jie and transport vice commissioner Wu Zeren took charge.

sentences.zh: 綖坐刺流海島，連坐者十餘人，時皆冤之。

translations.literal: Tuan sentenced to tattooing and exile to sea island; jointly implicated over ten persons—at the time all considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tuan was tattooed and exiled to an island; more than ten others were implicated, and many regarded the case as a miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 於是頒行大觀新修錢法於天下，申命開封府尹少、外路監司，各分州郡舉行，按舉能否，月檢會法令，使民知禁。

translations.literal: Thereupon promulgated Daguan newly revised coin law throughout the realm; reiterated ordering Kaifeng prefect and vice, outer circuit supervisory commissioners—each dividing prefectures to implement, investigating capability, monthly inspecting and collating laws, making the people know prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: The revised Daguan coin code was issued empire-wide. The Kaifeng prefect, his deputy, and circuit commissioners were told to enforce it locally, report performance monthly, and make prohibitions plain to the public.

sentences.zh: 用孫傑言，盜鑄依淮東重法地，囊橐強盜之家，籍其財以待賞，居停鄰保並均備告驗；

translations.literal: Using Sun Jie's words: illicit casting follow Huaidong heavy-law territory; bag-and-sack robber households—forfeit their property awaiting reward; lodging neighbors and mutual-responsibility groups all share reporting and verification;
translations.idiomatic: Following Sun Jie's advice, counterfeiting was placed under Huaidong's harshest statutes: robbers' assets were seized for rewards, and landlords and mutual-responsibility neighbors were bound to report and verify;

sentences.zh: 私錢依私茶法；

translations.literal: private coin follow private-tea law;
translations.idiomatic: private coin was punished under private-tea law;

sentences.zh: 給隨行物；

translations.literal: provide accompanying goods;
translations.idiomatic: informants were rewarded with goods seized in transit;

sentences.zh: 州常樁盜鑄賞錢五千緡，州縣稽於施行，監司失察，不以赦原。

translations.literal: Prefectures regularly stored illicit-casting reward money five thousand strings; prefectures and counties slow in implementation, supervisory commissioners failing inspection—not forgiven by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture maintained five thousand strings for counterfeiting rewards. Delayed enforcement or supervisory negligence was not pardonable.

sentences.zh: 是歲，京畿既置錢監，乃專鑄當十大錢，而小平錢則鑄於諸路。

translations.literal: This year, metropolitan region having established mints, then exclusively cast value-ten large coins, while small coins were cast in various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: That year capital mints produced only large value-ten coin; small coin was minted in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 既而當十錢少，復置真州鑄錢監，以本路所換錢不依式者及諸司當二見緡，用舊式改鑄當十錢。

translations.literal: Soon value-ten coins were few; again established Zhen Prefecture coin mint, using this circuit's exchanged coin not conforming to standard and various offices' value-two visible strings, using old standard to recast value-ten coins.
translations.idiomatic: When value-ten coin ran short, a mint opened at Zhenzhou to recoin nonstandard exchanged cash and offices' value-two holdings into value-ten on the old dies.

sentences.zh: 明年，令江、池、饒、建州錢監，自來歲以鑄當十五分鑄小平錢。

translations.literal: Next year, ordered Jiang, Chi, Rao, and Jian mints—from next year with five parts in ten cast small coins.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Jiang, Chi, Rao, and Jian mints were told that from the following year, five-tenths of output would be small coin.

sentences.zh: 申嚴私鑄之法，即托權要事勢，度越關津，拒捍搜索者，雖輕以違制論，載禦物者同之。

translations.literal: Further tightened illicit-casting laws: those relying on powerful connections and influence, crossing passes, resisting search—even lightly judged under violation-of-edict; those carrying imperial goods—the same.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiting laws were tightened again: using influence to cross checkpoints or resist search drew edict-violation charges even for lesser offenses, as did carrying imperial goods improperly.

sentences.zh: 初，崇寧五年，始禁陝西鐵錢行於興元府等界。

translations.literal: Initially, Chongning fifth year, first prohibited Shaanxi iron coins circulating in Xingyuan Prefecture and other borders.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 5, Shaanxi iron cash was first barred from Xingyuan Prefecture and neighboring borders.

sentences.zh: 至是，又以鐵錢猥多，禁陝西鐵錢入蜀。

translations.literal: At this time, again because iron coins were excessively many, prohibited Shaanxi iron coins entering Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Iron cash was now so abundant that Shaanxi iron coin was barred from entering Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 有董奎者，為走馬承受，遂令以鐵錢三折銅錢一。

translations.literal: There was one Dong Kui, serving as mounted courier commissioner, then ordered iron coins three-for-one copper coins.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted courier commissioner Dong Kui ordered iron cash revalued at three to one against copper.

sentences.zh: 事聞，責奎以妄肆胸臆，致幣輕物重，奎遂即罪。

translations.literal: Matter reported; rebuked Kui for recklessly venting personal opinion, causing coin light and goods heavy; Kui then immediately punished.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, Kui was blamed for arbitrary policy that debased coin and inflated prices, and was punished immediately.

sentences.zh: 三年，申當十錢行使之令，益以京東、京西，而河北並邊州縣鎮砦、四榷場及登、萊、密州緣海縣鎮等皆禁。

translations.literal: Third year, extended value-ten coin circulation order, adding Jingdong and Jingxi; while Hebei frontier prefectures, counties, fortresses, four border markets, and Deng, Lai, and Mi coastal counties and towns—all prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, value-ten coin was extended to Jingdong and Jingxi, but barred from Hebei border posts, the four border markets, and coastal counties of Deng, Lai, and Mi.

sentences.zh: 時蔡京復罷政矣。

translations.literal: At that time Cai Jing had again been removed from power.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing had fallen from power again by then.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔：「鼓鑄當十錢多，慮法隨以弊，其止鑄舊額小平錢。」

translations.literal: Fourth year, edict: "Hammer-casting value-ten coins is too much; fearing the law follows into debasement, stop casting and [only] old-quota small coins."
translations.idiomatic: In year four an edict declared: "Value-ten minting has grown excessive and threatens to ruin the system. Mint only the old small-coin quota."

sentences.zh: 張商英為相，奏言：「當十錢為害久矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Shangying as chief minister memorialized, saying: "Value-ten coins have harmed for long.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zhang Shangying wrote: "Value-ten coin has done harm for years.

sentences.zh: 舊小平錢有出門之禁，故四方客旅之貨，交易得錢，必大半入中末鹽鈔，收買告牒，而餘錢又流布在市井，此上下內外交相養。

translations.literal: Old small coins had exit prohibitions; therefore goods of travelers from four directions—obtaining cash from trade—must mostly enter intermediate and terminal salt notes, purchasing certificates; remaining cash again circulated in markets—this above and below, inner and outer, mutually sustained one another.
translations.idiomatic: Small coin once could not leave the circuit, so travelers' trade proceeds mostly went into salt-note deposits and certificate purchases, while surplus cash circulated in markets—a system that sustained court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 自當十錢行，以一夫而負八十千，小車載四百千，錢既為輕齎之物，則告牒為滯貨，鹽鈔非得虛抬之息則不行。

translations.literal: Since value-ten coins circulated, one man could carry eighty thousand, small cart load four hundred thousand; coin having become light-carry goods—then certificates became stagnant goods; salt notes unless obtaining falsely inflated interest would not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Value-ten coin made cash easy to transport—a man could carry eighty strings, a cart four hundred—turning certificates into dead stock and forcing salt notes to rely on artificial markups to move.

sentences.zh: 臣今欲借內庫並密院諸司封樁綢絹、金銀並鹽鈔，下令折十錢限民半年所在送官，十千給銀絹各一匹兩，限竟毋更用。

translations.literal: Your minister now wishes to borrow sealed silk and satin from the Inner Treasury together with the Privy Council's various offices, and gold, silver, and salt notes, issue an order to redeem value-ten coins—limit the people to half a year to deliver them locally to the government; for ten thousand [cash] give one bolt each of silk and satin; when the period ends, do not use them again.
translations.idiomatic: I propose borrowing sealed silk, gold, silver, and salt notes from the Inner Treasury and Privy Council stores and ordering value-ten coin redeemed within six months wherever people are located; for every ten thousand cash delivered, one bolt of silk and one of satin would be paid; once the period closed, those coins would cease circulating.

sentences.zh: 俟錢入官，擇其惡者鑄小平錢，存其好者折三行用。

translations.literal: Awaiting the coin entering government, select the bad ones to cast small coins, keep the good ones as value-three for circulation.
translations.idiomatic: Once the coin reached the treasury, the worst would be recoined as small cash and the soundest kept circulating at triple value.

sentences.zh: 如此則錢法、鈔法不相低昂，可以復舊。」

translations.literal: Thus then coin law and note law would not mutually rise and fall, and the old [system] could be restored."
translations.idiomatic: That way coin and note systems would no longer work at cross purposes, and the old order could be restored."

sentences.zh: 利州路提刑司言：「舊銅鐵錢輕重相尋，以大鐵錢一折小銅錢二；

translations.literal: Lizhou Circuit judicial commissioner reported: "Formerly copper and iron coins' light and heavy [values] followed one another, using one large iron coin exchanged for two small copper coins;
translations.idiomatic: The Lizhou judicial commissioner reported: "Under the old system, copper and iron cash traded at set weight ratios: one large iron coin counted as two small copper ones;

sentences.zh: 今大鐵錢五止當一銅錢，比舊輕十倍。

translations.literal: Now five large iron coins only equal one copper coin—compared with the old [rate], ten times lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Now five large iron coins buy only one copper coin—one-tenth the old weight in value.

sentences.zh: 又流入川界，錢輕物重，頗類陝西。

translations.literal: Moreover flowing into the Sichuan border—coin light, goods heavy—rather like Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: They also flooded into Sichuan, where coin was debased and prices inflated—much like Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 欲將折二大鐵錢以一折一，雖稍減錢數，錢必稍重。」

translations.literal: Wishing to take value-two large iron coins and exchange one for one; although slightly reducing coin count, coin would necessarily be slightly heavier."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed revaluing double iron cash one-for-one, which would reduce the quantity in circulation but increase each coin's effective weight.

sentences.zh: 詔許陝西鐵錢入蜀仍舊，盡釋其禁，且命以今物價量宜裁之。

translations.literal: Edict permitted Shaanxi iron coins entering Shu as before, completely releasing the prohibition, and ordered according to present commodity prices to weigh and appropriately adjust.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed Shaanxi iron cash into Sichuan again, lifting all restrictions and ordering an adjustment suited to current prices.

sentences.zh: 政和元年詔：「錢重則物輕，錢輕則物重，其勢然也。

translations.literal: Zhenghe first year edict: "When coin is heavy then goods are light; when coin is light then goods are heavy—the trend is necessarily so.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhenghe 1 edict observed: "Heavy coin lowers prices; light coin raises them—that is the natural tendency.

sentences.zh: 今諸路所鑄小平錢，行之久而無弊，多而不壅，為利博矣。

translations.literal: Now small coins cast in various circuits—circulated long without harm, many yet not obstructed—benefit is broad.
translations.idiomatic: Small coin minted in the provinces had circulated for years without trouble—plentiful yet not stagnant—to great benefit.

sentences.zh: 往歲圖利之臣鼓鑄當十錢，苟濟目前，不究悠久，公私為害，用之幾十年，其法日弊而不勝。

translations.literal: In past years profit-seeking ministers hammer-cast value-ten coins, merely relieving the present, not investigating the lasting; public and private harmed; used nearly several decades—its law daily debased yet could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Profit-minded officials had minted value-ten coin for short-term relief without regard for the long term, harming government and private alike; after decades in use the system grew daily more unsound.

sentences.zh: 奸猾之民規利冒法，銷毀當二、小平錢，所在盜鑄，濫錢益多，百物增價。

translations.literal: Crafty scheming commoners seeking profit violating law, melted value-two and small coins, everywhere illicitly cast—debased coin ever more, all goods increased price.
translations.idiomatic: Speculators melted down double and small coin and counterfeited everywhere, flooding the market with debased cash and driving up all prices.

sentences.zh: 若不早革，即弊無已時。

translations.literal: If not early reformed, then debasement without end-time.
translations.idiomatic: Without early reform, the debasement would never end.

sentences.zh: 其官私見在當十錢，可並作當三，以為定制。

translations.literal: Those public and private presently existing value-ten coins—may all be made value-three, establishing as fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: All value-ten coin held by government or private parties would be revalued at triple face value as the permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 尚慮豪猾憚於折閱，胥動浮言，可內自京尹，外逮監司、郡縣，悉心開諭。」

translations.literal: Still fearing powerful schemers dreading the reduction audit, all stirring empty talk—may internally from the capital prefect, externally reaching supervisory commissioners, prefectures and counties, wholeheartedly explain and instruct."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing wealthy speculators would resist the devaluation and spread rumors, the capital prefect, circuit commissioners, and local officials were told to explain the change carefully."

sentences.zh: 政和元年，錢輕物重，細民艱食，詔：「應陝西舊行使鐵錢地，並依元豐年大鐵錢折二，公私通行，夾錫錢同之，毋得分別。

translations.literal: Zhenghe first year, coin light goods heavy, common people hard-pressed for food, edict: "All old Shaanxi iron-coin-using territories—altogether follow Yuanfeng-era large iron coin value-two, public and private circulating, tin-mixed coins the same, must not distinguish separately.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 1, debased coin and high prices left commoners struggling to eat. An edict declared: "All former Shaanxi iron-cash zones would revert to Yuanfeng double iron cash, circulating alongside tin-mixed coin without distinction.

sentences.zh: 見存鐵錢，毋改更鑄夾錫，河東官私折二、夾錫錢同之。」

translations.literal: Presently stored iron coins—must not change or recast as tin-mixed; Hedong official and private value-two and tin-mixed coins—the same."
translations.idiomatic: Existing iron cash would not be recoined as tin-mixed; Hedong's double and tin-mixed coin would follow the same rule."

sentences.zh: 童貫宣撫陝西，以詔亟平物價，帥臣徐處仁切責其非，坐貶。

translations.literal: Tong Guan pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, using the edict urgently to level commodity prices; military commissioner Xu Churen sharply rebuked this as wrong, and was demoted on account.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan, the Shaanxi pacification commissioner, rushed to enforce the edict and stabilize prices. Military commissioner Xu Churen sharply criticized the policy and was demoted.

sentences.zh: 錢即經略鄜延，抗疏言：「詳考詔旨，謂鐵錢復行，與夾錫並用。

translations.literal: Qian Ji, Military Commissioner of Yan-Yan, submitted a memorial saying: "Examining in detail the edict's intent—it states iron coins restored to circulation, used together with tin-mixed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan-Yan military commissioner Qian Ji memorialized: "The edict's intent is to restore iron cash and circulate it alongside tin-mixed coin.

sentences.zh: 慮奸民妄作輕重，欲維持推行，俾錢物相直，非欲以威力脅製百姓，頓減物價於一兩月之間。

translations.literal: Fearing crafty commoners recklessly making light and heavy [values], wishing to maintain and implement, enabling coin and goods mutually equal—not wishing to use authority to coerce the common people, suddenly reducing commodity prices within one or two months.
translations.idiomatic: It aims to prevent manipulators from distorting exchange rates and to keep coin and goods at parity—not to force prices down overnight by imperial threats.

sentences.zh: 今宣撫司裁損米穀、布帛、金銀之價，殆非人情。

translations.literal: Now the pacification commission cut grain, cloth, gold and silver prices—hardly conforming to human sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification office's cuts to grain, cloth, gold, and silver prices defied common sense.

sentences.zh: 徐處仁言雖未盡，所見為長，望速詢其實。

translations.literal: Xu Churen's words though not exhaustive, his view is superior; hope quickly to inquire into the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Churen had not said all that needed saying, but his view was correct; I ask that the facts be investigated at once.

sentences.zh: 如臣言乖謬，願同處仁貶。」

translations.literal: If your minister's words are perverse, willing together with Churen to be demoted."
translations.idiomatic: If I am wrong, I ask to share Churen's punishment.

sentences.zh: 詔即妄有建明，毀辱使命，謫置偏州。

translations.literal: Edict: immediately—recklessly having proposals, insulting and shaming the mission—relegated to a remote prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court replied that he had presumptuously challenged policy and insulted the imperial mission, and banished him to a remote prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋亦罷行夾錫錢，且禁裁物價，民商貿易，各從其便。

translations.literal: Soon also abolished circulation of tin-mixed coins, and prohibited cutting commodity prices; common people and merchants trading—each follow their convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Tin-mixed coin was soon withdrawn, price controls were lifted, and trade was left to find its own level.

sentences.zh: 繼而童貫復請與舊法鐵錢並折二通行。

translations.literal: Subsequently Tong Guan again requested together with old-regulation iron coins all to circulate at value-two.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan then asked that tin-mixed coin circulate alongside old iron cash at double value.

sentences.zh: 知閿鄉縣論九齡俄坐以銅錢一估夾錫錢七八，並知州王寀、轉運副使張深俱被劾。

translations.literal: Wenxiang County magistrate Lun Jiuling soon on account of one copper coin valuing tin-mixed coins seven or eight—and prefect Wang Cai and transport vice commissioner Zhang Shen all impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang magistrate Lun Jiuling was soon impeached for pricing one copper coin at seven or eight tin-mixed coins; prefect Wang Cai and transport vice commissioner Zhang Shen were impeached as well.

sentences.zh: 時關中錢甚輕，夾錫欲以重之，其實與鐵錢等，物價日增，患甚於當十。

translations.literal: At the time Guanzhong coin was very light; tin-mixed wished to make it heavy—but in fact equal to iron coins; commodity prices daily increased; the affliction worse than value-ten.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong cash was badly debased; tin-mixed coin was meant to restore weight but proved no better than iron cash, and prices rose daily—a worse plague than value-ten coin.

sentences.zh: 二年，蔡京復得政，條奏廣、惠、康、賀、衡、鄂、舒州昨鑄夾錫錢精善，請復鑄如故。

translations.literal: Second year, Cai Jing again obtained power, itemized memorial that Guang, Hui, Kang, He, Heng, E, and Shu prefectures' formerly cast tin-mixed coins were fine and good—requested restore casting as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year two Cai Jing returned to power and reported that tin-mixed coin minted at Guang, Hui, Kang, He, Heng, E, and Shu was of excellent quality, asking that minting resume.

sentences.zh: 廣西、湖北、淮東如之，且命諸路以銅錢監復改鑄夾錫，遂以政和錢頒式焉。

translations.literal: Guangxi, Hubei, Huaidong—the same; and ordered various circuits' copper mints again to change cast tin-mixed; thereupon with Zhenghe coin issued the standard pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi, Hubei, and Huaidong followed suit; provincial copper mints were ordered to switch to tin-mixed coin, and the Zhenghe standard was issued.

sentences.zh: 夾錫錢既復推行，錢輕不與銅等，而法必欲其重，乃嚴擅易抬減之令。

translations.literal: Tin-mixed coins having again been implemented—coin light, not equal to copper—yet the law necessarily wanted them heavy; then strictly [enforced] unauthorized exchange, markup, and markdown orders.
translations.idiomatic: Once tin-mixed coin was restored, it was lighter than copper yet the law demanded it trade at par; unauthorized markups and discounts were sternly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 凡以金銀、絲帛等物貿易，有弗受夾錫、須要銅錢者，聽人告論，以法懲治。

translations.literal: Whenever trading gold, silver, silk, cloth and such goods—if not accepting tin-mixed, requiring copper coins—allow people to report and sue, punish by law.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone trading goods for gold, silver, or cloth who refused tin-mixed coin and demanded copper was subject to informants' lawsuits and legal punishment.

sentences.zh: 市井細民朝夕鬻餅餌熟食以自給者，或不免於告罰。

translations.literal: Market commoners morning and evening selling cakes and cooked food to sustain themselves—even they could not avoid reporting and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Street vendors who sold baked goods and cooked food for a living were sometimes prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以夾錫錢不以何路所鑄，並聽通行。

translations.literal: Before long, tin-mixed coins—not distinguishing which circuit cast them—all permitted to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon tin-mixed coin from any mint was allowed to circulate regardless of origin.

sentences.zh: 陝西用「政和通寶」舊大鐵錢，與夾錫錢雜。

translations.literal: Shaanxi used old "Zhenghe Tongbao" large iron coins, mixed with tin-mixed coins.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi still used old large Zhenghe Tongbao iron cash alongside tin-mixed coin.

sentences.zh: 慮流轉諸路，四年，詔毋更行用，致令諸監改鑄夾錫錢，在民間者赴官換納。

translations.literal: Fearing circulation to various circuits, fourth year, edict: do not further circulate and use; ordered various mints to change cast tin-mixed coins; those among the people—report to government and exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing these would spread to other circuits, in year four the old iron coins were withdrawn, mints recoined them as tin-mixed cash, and the public was ordered to turn holdings in.

sentences.zh: 鄭居中、劉正夫為相，以為不便，令淮南夾錫錢期三日官私俱禁不用，仍罷鼓鑄，夾錫錢悉輦樁關中。

translations.literal: Zheng Juzhong and Liu Zhengfu as chief ministers, deeming inconvenient, ordered Huainan tin-mixed coins within three days—official and private all forbidden not to use; still abolished hammer-casting; tin-mixed coins all carted and stored in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Zheng Juzhong and Liu Zhengfu found the policy impractical and gave Huainan three days to stop using tin-mixed coin, halted minting, and shipped all tin-mixed cash to Guanzhong for storage.

sentences.zh: 尋詔河東、陝西外，餘路並罷；

translations.literal: Soon edict: outside Hedong and Shaanxi, remaining circuits all abolished;
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon ended tin-mixed coin everywhere except Hedong and Shaanxi;

sentences.zh: 俄詔並河東罷鑄夾錫錢，止用舊法鼓鑄。

translations.literal: Shortly edict: together with Hedong abolished casting tin-mixed; only used old-regulation hammer-casting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hedong too ceased minting tin-mixed coin and reverted to the old iron-cash standard.

sentences.zh: 重和元年，權罷京西鑄夾錫錢，繼以關中糴買，用之通流，復命鼓鑄，專給關中。

translations.literal: Chonghe first year, temporarily abolished Jingxi casting tin-mixed; subsequently because Guanzhong grain purchases used them for general circulation, again ordered hammer-casting, exclusively supplying Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Chonghe 1 Jingxi tin-mixed minting was briefly halted; when Guanzhong grain procurement needed the coins, minting resumed to supply the region alone.

sentences.zh: 夾錫行，小民往往以藥點染，與銅錢相亂，河北漕臣張翬等嘗坐貶焉。

translations.literal: Tin-mixed circulating—common people often used drugs to stain and dye, mixing with copper coins; Hebei transport commissioner Zhang Hui and others once demoted on account.
translations.idiomatic: In circulation, commoners often dyed tin-mixed coin to pass it off as copper; Hebei transport commissioner Zhang Hui and others were once demoted over the problem.

sentences.zh: 先是，江池饒州、建寧府四監，歲鑄錢百三十四萬緡，充上供；

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiang, Chi, Rao prefectures and Jianning Prefecture—four mints—yearly cast coin 1.34 million strings, filling imperial tribute;
translations.idiomatic: Previously the four mints at Jiang, Chi, Rao, and Jianning cast 1.34 million strings yearly for imperial tribute;

sentences.zh: 衡、舒、嚴、鄂、韶、梧州六監，歲鑄錢百五十六萬緡，充逐路支用。

translations.literal: Heng, Shu, Yan, E, Shao, and Wu prefectures—six mints—yearly cast coin 1.56 million strings, filling each-circuit expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Six mints at Heng, Shu, Yan, E, Shao, and Wu cast 1.56 million strings for circuit expenses.

sentences.zh: 建炎經兵，鼓鑄皆廢。

translations.literal: Jianyan [era] suffered warfare; hammer-casting all abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: War during the Jianyan reign ended minting entirely.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，並廣寧監於虔州，並永豐監於饒州，歲鑄才及八萬緡。

translations.literal: Shaoxing early period, merged Guangning Mint into Qianzhou, merged Yongfeng Mint into Raozhou—yearly casting only reached eighty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing era Guangning Mint was merged into Qianzhou and Yongfeng into Raozhou; annual output fell to eighty thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 以銅、鐵、鉛、錫之入，不及於舊，而官吏稍廩工作之費，視前日自若也，每鑄錢一千，率用本錢二千四百文。

translations.literal: Because copper, iron, lead, and tin intake did not reach the old [levels], yet officials' slight rations and labor costs—compared with previous days as if unchanged—each casting one thousand coins on average used capital two thousand four hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: Copper, iron, lead, and tin supplies fell short of former levels, yet official salaries and labor costs stayed as high as before; minting one thousand coins now cost 2,400 cash in materials.

sentences.zh: 時範汝為作亂，權罷建州鼓鑄，尋復舊，泉司供給銅、錫六十五萬餘斤。

translations.literal: At the time Fan Ruwei rebelled; temporarily abolished Jianzhou hammer-casting; soon restored; the Coin Office supplied copper and tin over 650,000 jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Ruwei rebelled, the Jianzhou mint was briefly shut down but soon reopened; the Coin Office supplied over 650,000 jin of copper and tin.

sentences.zh: 六年，斂民間銅器，詔民私鑄銅器者徒二年。

translations.literal: Sixth year, collected the people's copper vessels; edict: common people privately casting copper vessels—two years hard labor.
translations.idiomatic: In year six private copperware was confiscated; unauthorized copper casting was punished with two years' penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 贛、饒二監新額錢四十萬緡，提點官趙伯瑜以為得不償費，罷鼓鑄，盡取木炭銅鉛本錢及官吏闕額衣糧水腳之屬，湊為年計。

translations.literal: Gan and Rao two mints' new quota coins four hundred thousand strings; intendant Zhao Boyu deemed gains not compensating costs, abolished hammer-casting, entirely took charcoal, copper, lead capital and officials' shortfall grain, clothing, transport costs and such—pooled as annual budget.
translations.idiomatic: The Gan and Rao mints had a quota of 400,000 strings; intendant Zhao Boyu found minting unprofitable and closed them, pooling charcoal, ore, salaries, and transport costs into a single annual budget instead.

sentences.zh: 十三年，韓球為使，復鑄新錢，興廢坑治，至於發塚墓，壞廬舍，籍冶戶姓名，以膽水盛時浸銅之數為額。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, Han Qiu as commissioner, again cast new coins, revived abandoned mines and smelters, reaching to opening tombs, destroying dwellings, registering smelter households' names, using gall-water peak-season copper-leaching quotas as the target.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen commissioner Han Qiu resumed minting, reopening mines and smelters—even opening graves and demolishing homes—and registered smelter households against gall-water leaching quotas at peak season.

sentences.zh: 〈（浸銅之法：以生鐵鍛成薄片，排置膽水槽中浸漬數日，鐵片為膽水所薄，上生赤煤，取刮鐵煤入爐，三煉成銅。

translations.literal: (Copper-leaching method: using raw iron forged into thin sheets, arranged and placed in gall-water troughs to soak several days; iron sheets thinned by gall-water, on top grew red ore; take and scrape iron ore into furnace, thrice smelted to become copper.
translations.idiomatic: (The leaching method: raw iron was hammered into thin plates and soaked in gall-water troughs for days until the iron thinned and red precipitate formed; the precipitate was scraped off and smelted three times to produce copper.

sentences.zh: 大率用鐵二斤四兩，得銅一斤。

translations.literal: Generally using iron two jin four liang, obtained copper one jin.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly two jin four liang of iron yielded one jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 饒州興利場、信州鉛山場各有歲額，所謂膽銅也。）〉

translations.literal: Raozhou Xingli field and Xinzhou Qianshan field each had annual quotas—what is called gall-copper.)
translations.idiomatic: Raozhou's Xingli works and Xinzhou's Qianshan works each had annual quotas—this was gall-copper.)

sentences.zh: 無銅可輸者，至熔錢為銅，然所鑄亦才及十萬緡。

translations.literal: Those with no copper to deliver—even to melting coins as copper; yet what was cast also only reached one hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could supply no copper even melted down coin for ore, yet output still reached only one hundred thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，罷鐵錢司歸之漕司。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth year, abolished Iron Coin Office, returned to Transport Office.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four the Iron Coin Office was abolished and its duties returned to the transport commission.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，出版曹錢八萬緡為鑄本，歲權以十五萬緡為額。

translations.literal: Twenty-seventh year, issued Board of Revenue funds eighty thousand strings as casting capital; yearly provisionally took one hundred fifty thousand strings as quota.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-seven the Board of Revenue released eighty thousand strings for mint capital and set a provisional annual quota of 150,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 復饒、贛、韶鑄錢監，以漕臣往來措置，通判主之。

translations.literal: Restored Rao, Gan, and Shao coin mints; transport commissioners coming and going to arrange; vice-prefects presiding.
translations.idiomatic: The Rao, Gan, and Shao mints were reopened under transport commissioners who supervised in rotation, with vice-prefects in charge.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史王珪言泉司不可廢，復以戶部侍郎榮薿提領，許置官屬二員。

translations.literal: Palace censor Wang Gui said the Coin Office could not be abolished; again appointed Households Vice Minister Rong Yi to oversee, permitted to establish two staff officials.
translations.idiomatic: Palace censor Wang Gui argued that the Coin Office must not be scrapped; Vice Minister of Revenue Rong Yi was reappointed to head it with two authorized staff.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，出禦府銅器千五百事付泉司，大索民間銅器，得銅二百餘萬斤，寺觀鍾、磬、鐃、鈸既籍定投稅外，不得添鑄。

translations.literal: Twenty-eighth year, issued imperial household copperware 1,500 pieces to Coin Office, searched broadly among people's copperware, obtained copper over two million jin; temple and monastery bells, chimes, cymbals, gongs—once registered fixed in tax—outside this, must not add casting.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight 1,500 imperial copper vessels went to the Coin Office and a sweeping collection of private copperware yielded over two million jin; temple bells and gongs already on the tax rolls could not be recast.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，令命官之家留見錢二萬貫，民庶半之，餘限二年聽轉易金銀，算請茶、鹽、香、礬鈔引之類，越數寄隱，許人告。

translations.literal: Twenty-ninth year, ordered official families keep on hand two wan guan cash, common people half that; remainder limit two years permitted to convert to gold and silver, purchase tea, salt, incense, alum note licenses and such; exceeding amounts concealed—permit people to report.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-nine official households could keep 20,000 strings in cash and commoners half that; surplus cash had two years to be converted to gold and silver or used to buy tea, salt, incense, and alum certificates; hoarding beyond the limit was reportable.

sentences.zh: 以李植提點鑄錢公事，植言：「歲額內藏庫二十三萬緡，右藏庫七十餘萬緡，皆至道以後數也。

translations.literal: Appointed Li Zhi intendant of coin-casting affairs; Zhi said: "Annual quota Inner Treasury 230,000 strings, Right Treasury over 700,000 strings—all Zhidao-era onward numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi was appointed coin intendant and reported: "The Inner Treasury quota was 230,000 strings and the Right Treasury over 700,000—figures dating from the Zhidao era onward.

sentences.zh: 紹興以來，歲收銅二十四萬斤，鉛二十萬斤，錫五百斤，僅可鑄錢一十萬緡。

translations.literal: Since Shaoxing, yearly collected copper 240,000 jin, lead 200,000 jin, tin 500 jin—barely able to cast one hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shaoxing, annual intake was 240,000 jin of copper, 200,000 of lead, and 500 of tin—enough for only 100,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 諸道拘到銅器二百萬斤，附以鉛、錫，可鑄六十萬緡。

translations.literal: Various circuits seized copperware two million jin; added lead and tin—could cast six hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Two million jin of confiscated copperware from the circuits, with lead and tin added, could yield 600,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 然拘者不可以常，唯當據坑冶所產。」

translations.literal: Yet seized goods cannot be regular; only ought to rely on mine and smelter output."
translations.idiomatic: But seizures are countless on permanently; only mine and smelter output is reliable.

sentences.zh: 下工部，權以五十萬緡為額。

translations.literal: Referred to Works Ministry; provisionally took five hundred thousand strings as quota.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Works Ministry, which set a provisional quota of 500,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 又明年，才鑄及十萬緡。

translations.literal: Again next year, only cast reaching one hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: The following year output reached only 100,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 今泉司歲額增至十五萬緡，小平錢一萬八千緡，折二錢六萬六千緡。

translations.literal: Now Coin Office annual quota increased to one hundred fifty thousand strings—small coins eighteen thousand strings, value-two coins sixty-six thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: The Coin Office quota was now 150,000 strings—18,000 in small coin and 66,000 in double-value coin.

sentences.zh: 歲費鑄本及起綱糜費約二十六萬緡，司屬之費又約二萬緡，東南十一路一百一十八州之所供，有坑冶課利錢、木炭錢、錫本錢，約二十一萬緡，比歲所收不過十五六萬緡耳。

translations.literal: Yearly cost of casting capital and convoy expenses about 260,000 strings; office staff costs again about 20,000 strings; southeast eleven circuits' 118 prefectures' supplies—mining levy funds, charcoal funds, tin capital funds—about 210,000 strings; compared with yearly collections not exceeding 150,000–160,000 strings.
translations.idiomatic: Minting and transport cost about 260,000 strings yearly, office expenses another 20,000; levies from 118 prefectures in eleven southeastern circuits—mining taxes, charcoal fees, and tin subsidies—brought in only 150,000–160,000 of the expected 210,000.

sentences.zh: 歲額：金一百二十八兩，銀無額，以七分入內庫，三分歸本司，銅三十九萬五千八百斤，鉛三十七萬七千九百斤，錫一萬九千八百七十五斤，鐵二百三十二萬八千斤，比歲所榷十無二三。

translations.literal: Annual quota: gold 128 taels, silver no quota—seven-tenths enter Inner Treasury, three-tenths return to this office; copper 395,800 jin, lead 377,900 jin, tin 19,875 jin, iron 2,328,000 jin—compared with yearly collections, two or three out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Annual quotas called for 128 taels of gold (silver had none; seven-tenths of gold went to the Inner Treasury and three-tenths to the office), 395,800 jin of copper, 377,900 of lead, 19,875 of tin, and 2,328,000 of iron—but collections typically reached only two or three tenths of quota.

sentences.zh: 每當二錢千，重四斤五兩；

translations.literal: Each value-two thousand coins, weight four jin five liang;
translations.idiomatic: One thousand double-value coins weighed four jin five liang;

sentences.zh: 小平錢千，重四斤十三兩；

translations.literal: Small coins thousand, weight four jin thirteen liang;
translations.idiomatic: one thousand small coins weighed four jin thirteen liang;

sentences.zh: 視舊制，銅少鉛多，錢愈鍥薄矣。

translations.literal: Compared with old regulations—less copper, more lead—coins ever more stamped thin.
translations.idiomatic: compared with the old standard they contained less copper and more lead, and the coins grew ever thinner.

sentences.zh: 孝宗隆興元年，詔鑄當二、小平錢，如紹興之初。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong Longxing first year, edict cast value-two and small coins as at Shaoxing's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: In Longxing 1 Emperor Xiaozong ordered double and small coin minted as in early Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 〈（乾、淳迄於嘉泰、開禧皆如之。）〉

translations.literal: (From Qian, Chun through Jiatai and Kaixi—all the same.)
translations.idiomatic: (The same held from the Qian and Chun reigns through Jiatai and Kaixi.)

sentences.zh: 乾道六年，並鑄錢司歸發運司，尋復置。

translations.literal: Qiandao sixth year, merged Coin Office into Transport Commission; soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 6 the Coin Office was merged into the transport commission, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 八年，饒州、贛州復名置提點官。

translations.literal: Eighth year, Raozhou and Ganzhou again by name established intendant officials.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Raozhou and Ganzhou intendant posts were formally reestablished.

sentences.zh: 以新鑄錢殽雜，提點鑄錢及永平監官、左藏西庫監官、戶部工部長貳官責降有差。

translations.literal: Because newly cast coins were adulterated, coin intendant and Yongping Mint officials, Left Treasury West Depot officials, Households and Works vice ministers—all demoted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Adulterated new coin led to demotions for the coin intendant, Yongping Mint staff, Left Treasury West Depot officials, and vice ministers of Revenue and Works.

sentences.zh: 九年，大江之西及湖、廣間多毀錢，夾以沙泥重鑄，號「沙尾錢」，詔嚴禁之。

translations.literal: Ninth year, west of the Great River and between Hunan and Guang—many destroyed coins, mixed with sand and mud recast, called "sand-tail coins"—edict strictly prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine west of the Yangzi and across Hunan and Guangdong, worn coin was mixed with sand and mud and recast as "sand-tail cash," which an edict strictly forbade.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，並贛司歸饒州。

translations.literal: Chunxi second year, merged Gan office into Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 2 the Gan prefecture office was merged into Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 慶元三年，復禁銅器，期兩月鬻於官，每兩三十。

translations.literal: Qingyuan third year, again prohibited copper vessels; set period two months to sell to government; each liang thirty [cash].
translations.idiomatic: In Qingyuan 3 copperware was banned again; owners had two months to sell it to the government at thirty cash per liang.

sentences.zh: 湖州舊鬻監，至是官自鑄之。

translations.literal: Huzhou old Yujian Mint, at this time government itself cast them.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhou's former Yujian Mint was taken over for official coining.

sentences.zh: 〈（二年，禁銷錢為銅器者，以違制論，爐戶決配海外。）〉

translations.literal: (Second year, prohibited melting coins for copper vessels—judged under violation of edict; furnace households sentenced to exile overseas.)
translations.idiomatic: (In year two, melting coin for copperware was punished as an edict violation; smelter households were exiled overseas.)

sentences.zh: 復神泉監，以所括銅器鑄當三大錢，隸工部。

translations.literal: Restored Shenquan Mint, using confiscated copperware to cast value-three large coins, subordinate to Works Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Shenquan Mint was restored to cast triple-value coin from confiscated copperware under the Works Ministry.

sentences.zh: 舊額，內帑歲收新錢一百五萬，

translations.literal: Old quota—Inner Privy yearly received new coins one million five hundred thousand,
translations.idiomatic: Under the old quota the Inner Privy took in 1.5 million strings of new coin yearly,

sentences.zh: 〈（江、池、饒、建四監。）〉

translations.literal: (Jiang, Chi, Rao, Jian four mints.)
translations.idiomatic: (from the four mints at Jiang, Chi, Rao, and Jian.)

sentences.zh: 而每年退卻六十萬，三年一郊，又以一百萬輸三司，是內帑年才得十一萬六千餘緡，而左藏得九十三萬三千餘緡。

translations.literal: Yet yearly returned six hundred thousand; every three years one suburban sacrifice, again one million submitted to Three Departments—thus Inner Privy yearly only obtained over 116,000 strings, while Left Treasury obtained over 933,000 strings.
translations.idiomatic: But 600,000 strings were returned each year, and every three years a suburban sacrifice took one million for the Three Departments—leaving the Inner Privy only about 116,000 strings annually and the Left Treasury about 933,000.

sentences.zh: 今歲額止十五萬，而隸封樁者半，內藏者半，左藏咸無焉。

translations.literal: Now yearly quota only one hundred fifty thousand—half subordinate to sealed reserves, half Inner Treasury—Left Treasury entirely none.
translations.idiomatic: The quota was now only 150,000 strings, split evenly between sealed reserves and the Inner Treasury, with nothing for the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 淮南舊鑄銅錢。

translations.literal: Huainan formerly cast copper coins.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan had once minted copper cash.

sentences.zh: 乾道初，詔兩淮、京西悉用鐵錢。

translations.literal: Qiandao early, edict: Lianghuai and Jingxi entirely use iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiandao iron cash was ordered for all of the Huai region and Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 荊門隸湖北，以地接襄、峴，亦用鐵錢。

translations.literal: Jingmen subordinate to Hubei—as territory adjoins Xiang and Xian, also uses iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmen in Hubei, bordering Xiangyang and its approaches, used iron cash as well.

sentences.zh: 六年，先是，以和州舊有錢監，舒州山口鎮亦有古監，詔司農丞許子中往淮西措置。

translations.literal: Sixth year—earlier, because Hezhou formerly had a coin mint, Shuzhou Shankou town also had an ancient mint—edict Agriculture Vice Director Xu Zizhong go to Huaixi to arrange.
translations.idiomatic: In year six—Hezhou still had an old mint and Shuzhou's Shankou town an ancient one—Agriculture Vice Director Xu Zizhong was sent to organize minting in the Huai west.

sentences.zh: 於是子中以舒、蘄、黃皆產鐵，請各置監，

translations.literal: Thereupon Zizhong because Shu, Qi, and Huang all produced iron, requested each establish a mint,
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zizhong reported that Shu, Qi, and Huang prefectures all had iron and asked for a mint in each,

sentences.zh: 〈（舒州同安監，蘄州新春監，黃州齊安監。）〉

translations.literal: (Shuzhou Tong'an Mint, Qizhou Xinchun Mint, Huangzhou Qi'an Mint.)
translations.idiomatic: (Tong'an at Shuzhou, Xinchun at Qizhou, and Qi'an at Huangzhou.)

sentences.zh: 且鑄折二錢。

translations.literal: And cast value-two coins.
translations.idiomatic: They would mint double-value iron coin.

sentences.zh: 以發運司通領四監。

translations.literal: Using Transport Commission to oversee all four mints.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commission was given general oversight of all four mints.

sentences.zh: 〈（江之廣寧監，興國之大冶監，臨江之豐餘監，撫之裕國監。）〉

translations.literal: (Jiang's Guangning Mint, Xingguo's Daye Mint, Linjiang's Fengyu Mint, Fu's Yuguo Mint.)
translations.idiomatic: (Guangning in Jiangzhou, Daye in Xingguo, Fengyu in Linjiang, and Yuguo in Fuzhou.)

sentences.zh: 子中所領三監，歲合認三十萬貫，其大小鐵錢，令兩淮通行。

translations.literal: Zizhong's supervised three mints, yearly combined quota three hundred thousand strings—their large and small iron coins, ordered Lianghuai circulated generally.
translations.idiomatic: The three mints under Xu Zizhong were assigned a combined annual quota of 300,000 strings; their iron cash, large and small, was to circulate throughout the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 七年，舒、蘄守臣皆以鑄錢增美遷官，然淮民為之大擾。

translations.literal: Seventh year—Shu and Qi prefectural officials all because coin casting increase achieved promotion; yet Huai people because of this greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven the prefects of Shu and Qi were promoted for exceeding mint quotas, but the people of the Huai region were gravely troubled.

sentences.zh: 八年，以江州、興國軍鐵冶額虧，守貳及大冶知縣各降一官。

translations.literal: Eighth year—because Jiangzhou and Xingguo Circuit iron smelting quotas fell short, prefect and vice and Daye county magistrate each reduced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight, after Jiangzhou and Xingguo failed to meet iron-smelting quotas, the prefect and vice-prefect of each and the magistrate of Daye were each demoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年，詔舒州歲增鑄十萬貫，以三十萬貫為額；

translations.literal: Chunxi fifth year—edict: Shuzhou yearly increase cast one hundred thousand strings, with three hundred thousand strings as quota;
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi year five an edict raised Shuzhou's annual minting by 100,000 strings, setting its quota at 300,000;

sentences.zh: 蘄州增鑄五萬貫，以十五萬貫為額。

translations.literal: Qizhou increase cast fifty thousand strings, with one hundred fifty thousand strings as quota.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhou's minting was raised by 50,000 strings, with a quota of 150,000.

sentences.zh: 如更增鑄，優與推賞。

translations.literal: If further increase casting, favorably grant rewards and promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who cast still more were to receive generous rewards and promotions.

sentences.zh: 御史黃洽言：「興天下之利者，不窮天下之力。

translations.literal: Censor Huang Qia said: "Those who benefit the realm should not exhaust the realm's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Huang Qia said: "Those who seek profit for the empire must not exhaust the empire's resources.

sentences.zh: 舒、蘄歲鑄四十五萬不易為也。

translations.literal: Shu and Qi yearly cast four hundred fifty thousand—not easy to accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: An annual output of 450,000 strings from Shu and Qi together would not be easy to sustain.

sentences.zh: 又有增鑄之賞，恐其難繼。」

translations.literal: Moreover there are increase-casting rewards—feared it hard to continue."
translations.idiomatic: With bonuses offered for further increases, I fear the policy could not last.

sentences.zh: 詔除之。

translations.literal: Edict abolished them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict cancelled the bonuses.

sentences.zh: 八年，以舒州水遠，薪炭不便，減額五萬貫。

translations.literal: Eighth year—because Shuzhou water distant, fuel and charcoal inconvenient, reduced quota fifty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Shuzhou's quota was cut by 50,000 strings because its distance from water made fuel and charcoal hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 明年，又減十萬貫，與蘄州並以十五萬貫為額。

translations.literal: Next year, again reduced one hundred thousand strings—with Qizhou alike set one hundred fifty thousand strings as quota.
translations.idiomatic: The next year another 100,000 strings were cut, leaving both Shuzhou and Qizhou with quotas of 150,000 each.

sentences.zh: 十年，並舒州之宿城監入同安監。

translations.literal: Tenth year—merged Shuzhou's Sucheng Mint into Tong'an Mint.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten Shuzhou's Sucheng mint was merged into Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔舒、蘄鑄鐵錢，並增五萬貫，以「淳熙通寶」為文。

translations.literal: Twelfth year—edict: Shu and Qi cast iron coins, both increase fifty thousand strings, with "Chunxi Tongbao" as inscription.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve Shu and Qi were ordered to mint iron cash, each adding 50,000 strings bearing the legend "Chunxi Tongbao."

sentences.zh: 光宗紹熙二年，減蘄春、同安兩監歲鑄各十萬貫。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangzong Shaoxi second year—reduced Qichun and Tong'an two mints yearly casting each one hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi year two of Emperor Guangzong, annual output at the Qichun and Tong'an mints was cut by 100,000 strings each.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰三年，罷舒、蘄鼓鑄；

translations.literal: Jiatai third year—abolished Shu and Qi smelting and casting;
translations.idiomatic: In Jiatai year three minting at Shu and Qi was halted;

sentences.zh: 開禧三年，復之。

translations.literal: Kaixi third year—restored them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaixi year three it was restored.

sentences.zh: 嘉定五年，臣僚言江北以銅錢一折鐵錢四，禁之。

translations.literal: Jiading fifth year—officials said north of the river used one copper coin to exchange for four iron coins—prohibited it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading year five officials reported that north of the Yangzi one copper cash was traded for four iron and asked that this be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 時銅錢之在江北者，自乾道以來，悉以鐵錢易之，或以會子一貫易銅錢一貫。

translations.literal: At the time copper coins in Jiangbei—from Qiandao onward—all exchanged with iron coins, or sometimes one string of huizi exchanged for one string of copper coins.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qiandao, copper cash in the north had all been exchanged for iron, sometimes one string of huizi for one string of copper.

sentences.zh: 其銅錢輸送行在及建康、鎮江府。

translations.literal: That copper coin was transported to the mobile capital and Jiankang and Zhenjiang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The copper was shipped to the court, Jiankang, and Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 凡沿江私度及邊徑嚴禁漏泄，及於邊界三里內立堠，如出界法；

translations.literal: All along the river private ferry crossings and border paths strictly prohibited leakage; at border within three li erected beacon mounds, as border-crossing law;
translations.idiomatic: Private crossings along the river and smuggling routes were strictly barred, and within three li of the frontier beacon posts were set up under the laws against export;

sentences.zh: 其易京西銅錢，如兩淮例。

translations.literal: As for exchanging Jingxi copper coins, follow Lianghuai precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Copper in Jingxi was exchanged on the same terms as in the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 京西、湖北之鐵錢，則取給於漢陽監及興國富民監，後並富民監於漢陽監，以二十萬為額。

translations.literal: Jingxi and Hubei iron coins—then obtained from Hanyang Mint and Xingguo Fumin Mint; later merged Fumin Mint into Hanyang Mint, with two hundred thousand as quota.
translations.idiomatic: Iron cash for Jingxi and Hubei came from the Hanyang and Xingguo Fumin mints; Fumin was later merged into Hanyang, with a quota of 200,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 前宋時，川、陝皆行鐵錢，益、利、夔皆即山冶鑄。

translations.literal: Former Song times—Chuan and Shanxi all circulated iron coins; Yi, Li, and Kui all smelted at the mountains on site.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier Song times Sichuan and Shaanxi had used iron cash, with Yi, Li, and Kui circuits smelting on the spot from local ore.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，詔陝西諸路復行鐵錢。

translations.literal: Shaoxing ninth year—edict: Shaanxi various circuits restored circulating iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing year nine an edict restored iron cash in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十五年，置利州紹興監，鑄錢十萬緡以救錢引。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year—established Lizhou Shaoxing Mint, cast coins one hundred thousand strings to rescue qianyin.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen the Shaoxing mint at Lizhou was established to cast 100,000 strings and relieve the qianyin notes.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，復嘉之豐遠、邛之惠民二監，鑄小平錢。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year—restored Jia's Fengyuan and Qiong's Huimin two mints, cast small standard coins.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two the Fengyuan mint in Jiazhou and the Huimin mint in Qiongzhou were reopened to cast standard small cash.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，詔利州並鑄折二錢，後又鑄折二錢。

translations.literal: Twenty-third year—edict Lizhou also cast value-two coins; later again cast value-two coins.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three Lizhou was also ordered to mint double-value coin; double-value coin was minted again later.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十五年，四川餉臣言：「諸州行使兩界錢引，全籍鐵錢稱提，止有利州紹興監歲鑄折三錢三萬四千五百貫有奇，邛州惠民監歲鑄折三錢一萬二千五百貫。

translations.literal: Chunxi fifteenth year—Sichuan supply commissioner said: "Various prefectures circulate two-zone qianyin—all rely on iron coins for pegging; only Lizhou Shaoxing Mint yearly casts value-three coins thirty-four thousand five hundred strings odd, Qiongzhou Huimin Mint yearly casts value-three coins twelve thousand five hundred strings.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi year fifteen the Sichuan supply commissioner reported: "Prefectures circulating qianyin notes for both zones depend entirely on iron cash to back them; only the Shaoxing mint at Lizhou produces about 34,500 strings of triple-value coin annually, and the Huimin mint at Qiongzhou about 12,500 strings.

sentences.zh: 今大安軍淳熙、新興、迎恩三爐，出生鐵四十九萬五千斤，利之昭化、嘉川縣亦有爐，新產鐵三十餘萬斤。

translations.literal: Now Da'an Circuit Chunxi, Xinxing, and Ying'en three furnaces produce raw iron four hundred ninety-five thousand jin; Li's Zhaohua and Jiachuan counties also have furnaces, newly produce iron three hundred thousand-plus jin.
translations.idiomatic: The three furnaces at Chunxi, Xinxing, and Ying'en in Da'an produce 495,000 jin of pig iron, and furnaces in Zhaohua and Jiachuan in Lizhou have recently yielded more than 300,000 jin.
