translations.literal: Request permission to smelt and cast."
translations.idiomatic: We ask leave to begin minting.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，即利州鑄當五大錢。

translations.literal: Jiading first year—immediately at Lizhou cast worth-five large coins.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading year one Lizhou at once began minting five-for-one large coins.

sentences.zh: 三年，製司欲盡收舊引，又於紹興、惠民二監歲鑄三十萬貫，其料並同當三錢。

translations.literal: Third year—Pacification Commission wished entirely collect old notes; again at Shaoxing and Huimin two mints yearly cast three hundred thousand strings—their material all same as worth-three coins.
translations.idiomatic: In year three the Pacification Commission sought to retire all old notes and ordered the Shaoxing and Huimin mints to cast 300,000 strings annually, all using the same alloy as triple-value coin.

sentences.zh: 若四川銅錢，淳熙間易送湖廣總所儲之，後又交卸於江陵。

translations.literal: As for Sichuan copper coins—during Chunxi exchanged and sent to Huguang General Office for storage; later again delivered at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's copper cash, during Chunxi, had been exchanged and stored at the Huguang general depot and later transferred to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 寶慶元年，新錢以「大宋元寶」為文。

translations.literal: In Baoqing 1, the new coins bore the inscription "Da Song yuanbao."
translations.idiomatic: In Baoqing 1, the new coins bore the inscription "Da Song yuanbao."

sentences.zh: 端平元年，以膽銅所鑄之錢不耐久，舊錢之精致者泄於海舶，申嚴下海之禁。

translations.literal: In Duanping 1, because coins cast from cementation copper were not durable and the finer old coins were leaking out through seagoing ships, the prohibition on going to sea was reiterated and tightened.
translations.idiomatic: In Duanping 1, coins cast from cementation copper proved short-lived, while the finer old coins were flowing out through seagoing ships, so the ban on maritime export was reiterated and tightened.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙元年，新錢當二並小平錢並以「嘉熙通寶」為文，當三錢以「嘉熙重寶」為文。

translations.literal: In Jiaxi 1, the new two-cash coins and small standard coins both bore the inscription "Jiaxi tongbao," while the three-cash coins bore the inscription "Jiaxi zhongbao."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaxi 1, the new two-cash coins and small standard coins both bore the inscription "Jiaxi tongbao," while the three-cash coins read "Jiaxi zhongbao."

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，右諫議大夫劉晉之言：「巨家停積，猶可以發泄；

translations.literal: Chunyou fourth year—Right Remonstrance Grandee Liu Jin said: "Great households hoarding accumulation—still can be released;
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou year four Right Remonstrance Grandee Liu Jin said: "Hoarding by great families can still be drawn out;

sentences.zh: 銅器鉟銷，猶可以上遏；

translations.literal: Copper vessels melted down—still can be blocked from above;
translations.idiomatic: melting copperware can still be checked from above;

sentences.zh: 唯一入海舟，往而不返。」

translations.literal: Only the ships entering the sea—go and do not return."
translations.idiomatic: only ships that sail overseas depart and never come back.

sentences.zh: 於是復申嚴漏泄之禁。

translations.literal: Thereupon again strictly enforced prohibition on leakage.
translations.idiomatic: The prohibition on export was then enforced anew.

sentences.zh: 八年，監察御史陳求魯言：「議者謂楮便於運轉，故錢廢於蟄藏；

translations.literal: Eighth year—Investigating Censor Chen Qiulu said: "Discussants say paper notes convenient for transport, therefore coins abandoned in hoarding;
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Investigating Censor Chen Qiulu said: "Some argue that because paper notes are easy to move, coin is left idle in hoards;

sentences.zh: 自稱提之屢更，圜法為無用。

translations.literal: Since pegging repeatedly changed, coin law became useless.
translations.idiomatic: and that repeated changes in backing have made the coin system useless.

sentences.zh: 急於扶楮者，至嗾盜賊以窺人之閫奧，峻刑法以發人之窖藏，然不思患在於錢之荒，而不在於錢之積。

translations.literal: Those eager to support paper notes—reached to incite robbers to spy on people's inner chambers, severe punishments to expose people's hidden stores—yet did not consider the trouble lay in coin scarcity, not in coin accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: In their haste to prop up notes they incite thieves to pry into private stores and apply harsh law to force out hidden hoards, yet they never see that the problem is shortage of coin, not accumulation of it.

sentences.zh: 夫錢貴則物宜賤，今物與錢俱重，此一世之所共憂也。

translations.literal: When coins dear then goods should be cheap—now goods and coins both heavy—this one generation's shared worry.
translations.idiomatic: When money is dear, goods ought to be cheap; now both goods and money are costly—the whole age shares this worry.

sentences.zh: 蕃舶巨艘，形若山嶽，乘風駕浪，深入遐陬。

translations.literal: Foreign ships great vessels—form like mountains; riding wind, driving waves, deeply enter distant corners.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign merchant ships, huge as hills, ride the wind and waves deep into distant seas.

sentences.zh: 販於中國者皆浮靡無用之異物，而泄於外夷者乃國家富貴之操柄。

translations.literal: Sold in China—all frivolous useless exotic things; leaked to outer barbarians—precisely the state's wealth and honor's leverage.
translations.idiomatic: What they sell here is useless luxury; what leaks abroad is the very leverage of the state's wealth.

sentences.zh: 所得幾何，所失者不可勝計矣。

translations.literal: What obtained—how much? What lost—cannot be fully counted.
translations.idiomatic: The gain is slight; the loss is beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 京城之銷金，衢、信之鍮器，醴、泉之樂具，皆出於錢。

translations.literal: Capital's gilding, Qu and Xin's brassware, Li and Quan's musical instruments—all come from coins.
translations.idiomatic: Gilding in the capital, brassware in Quzhou and Xinzhou, musical instruments in Lizhou and Quanzhou—all consume coin.

sentences.zh: 臨川、隆興、桂林之銅工，尤多於諸郡。

translations.literal: Linchuan, Longxing, Guilin copper artisans—especially many among all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Copper smiths in Linchuan, Longxing, and Guilin outnumber those in other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 姑以長沙一郡言之，烏山銅爐之所六十有四，麻潭鵝羊山銅戶數百餘家，錢之不壞於器物者無幾。

translations.literal: For example take Changsha one prefecture—Wushan copper furnace places sixty-four; Matan E'yangshan copper households several hundred families; coins not destroyed in vessels—few indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Take Changsha alone: sixty-four copper-smelting sites at Wushan and several hundred smelting households at Matan and E'yangshan—little coin escapes being made into goods.

sentences.zh: 今京邑鍮銅器用之類，鬻賣公行於都市。

translations.literal: Now capital brass and copper vessels and such—sold openly in market cities.
translations.idiomatic: Yet brass and copper goods are now sold openly in the capital's markets.

sentences.zh: 畿甸之近，一繩以法，由內及外，觀聽聿新，則鉟銷之奸知畏矣。

translations.literal: Capital vicinity near—one rule with law, from inner to outer, observers' hearing entirely renewed—then melting-down wrongdoers would know fear.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the law first in the capital vicinity and extend it outward; once example is made, those who melt coin for vessels will fear to offend.

sentences.zh: 香、藥、象、犀之類異物之珍奇可悅者，本無適用之實，服御之間昭示儉德，自上化下，風俗丕變，則漏泄之弊少息矣。

translations.literal: Incense, medicines, ivory, rhinoceros horn and such exotic rarities pleasing—originally no practical use; in attire and service display frugality—above transforms below, customs greatly change—then leakage evils slightly cease.
translations.idiomatic: Exotics such as incense, medicines, ivory, and rhinoceros horn have no real use; thrift shown in dress and ceremony, transforming custom from above, would lessen the evil of export.

translations.literal: This is the way to rectify the root and clarify the source."
translations.idiomatic: That is the way to treat the root and clear the source.

sentences.zh: 有旨從之。

translations.literal: There was an edict: comply.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.
